https://tran.house.gov/media/press-relea: Washington, D.C. – This week, ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) joined a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins opposing a new proposed rule that would kick an estimated 6.3 million Americans – primarily older or disabled beneficiaries and families with children – off the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). Across the state, over 600,000 Californians would be at risk of losing SNAP benefits as a result of this proposed rule. “This rule would cut 6.3 million Americans off of the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) by rolling back a policy Congress created to permit states to extend SNAP food assistance to households that receive Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF)-funded benefits. This is contrary to federal law and would make life harder for millions of families. As the cost of groceries and other basic needs continue to rise, the Trump administration has made life less affordable for everyday Americans,” Representative Tran and his colleagues wrote in the letter. Food insecurity affects roughly 1 in 5 people in California, making SNAP a critical issue for families across Orange and LA County. According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture, there are over 27,000 households that receive SNAP in California's 45th District, 1.4 million residents that benefit from CalFresh food assistance programs in Los Angeles County, and over 300,000 residents that receive benefits in Orange County. With critical food assistance on the chopping block, Rep. Tran is fighting to make life easier for families ahead of the holidays. 214 House Democrats signed the letter, led by House Committee on Agriculture Ranking Member Representative Angie Craig. Under President Trump and Secretary Rollins, food insecurity in America has increased, according to independent analysis . Food inflation accelerated in October. Thanksgiving staples are up 11 percent year-over-year, outpacing inflation. Representative Tran is committed to ensuring that every family can afford the nutritious food they need to stay healthy: Rep. Tran co-sponsored the Keep SNAP and WIC Funded Act of 2025 , which would prevent the Trump administration from illegally withholding available funds for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC). Rep. Tran co-sponsored the Restoring Food Security for American Families and Farmers Act of 2025 , which would repeal cuts to SNAP from the Republican-led budget for 2026. Rep. Tran signed a discharge petition in the House to bring H.R. 2753, the Hands Off Medicaid and SNAP Act , to the House floor for a vote. In October 2025 , Representative Tran led a letter to Secretary of Agriculture, Brooke Rollins, fighting the lapse of SNAP benefits due to the government shutdown. He also voted against H.R. 1, Republicans’ so-called ‘Big Beautiful Bill,' which drastically slashed funding for SNAP. Washington, D.C. – This week, ahead of President Trump and President Xi Jinping’s meeting in China, U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) led a letter to President Trump demanding the release of $15.3 billion in security assistance for Taiwan. This critical funding will shore up Taiwan’s defense capabilities and aid the United States in continuing our longstanding diplomatic partnership with Taiwan. “Our commitment to supporting Taiwan’s security helps to promote the political, security, and economic interests of the United States. The continued delay of funding and defense packages to Taiwan jeopardizes these interests. As such, we urge you to maintain our commitment to Taiwan during conversations with President Xi, obligate the funds approved by Congress for Foreign Military Financing and the Taiwan Security Cooperation Initiative, and submit the $14 billion package of Foreign Military Sales for formal Congressional approval as soon as possible,” Representative Tran and his colleagues wrote in the letter. The United States’ relationship with Taiwan has long been based on the Taiwan Relations Act and the Six Assurances to Taiwan, a foundation that guides U.S. commitment to regional peace and shapes our security relationship with Taiwan. This relationship includes providing defensive arms to strengthen Taiwan's self-defense. In accordance with this policy, Congress appropriated $1.3 billion in security assistance for Taiwan last year; however, the Trump Administration has yet to release the funds. This $1.3 billion is in addition to a $14 billion package that the Administration signaled to Congress in January but has failed to move forward. Alongside Rep. Tran, the letter was also signed by Representatives Wesley Bell (MO-01), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Dave Min (CA-47), Pat Ryan (NY-18), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25), Jill Tokuda (HI-2), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Tom Suozzi (NY-03), Jim Costa (CA-21), André Carson (IN-07), Ted Lieu (CA-36), and Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06). As a member of the powerful House Armed Services Committee and the Congressional Taiwan Caucus, Representative Tran is committed to upholding peace and security in the Pacific and strengthening the U.S. partnership with Taiwan: Rep. Tran cosponsored the Taiwan Representative Office Act, which renames the “Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office” to the “Taiwan Representative Office,” reaffirming U.S. support for Taiwan. Rep. Tran also cosponsored the Taiwan and American Space Assistance Act, which expands the authority of NASA and NOAA to cooperate directly with the Taiwan Space Agency for civilian space activities. Washington, DC – Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) released the following statement following the House Democratic Caucus leadership election. With an overwhelming majority, Hakeem Jeffries was voted to be the Democratic nominee for the Speaker of the House of Representatives for the 120th Congress: “Over a week ago, the American people made their voices heard and called for Democratic leadership to stop the corruption, forge a new chapter for this country and fight for a better future. Moments like these call for strong, tested leadership. Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries has proven time and time again that he is ready to answer that call, and lead our country and our party into this new chapter. As a proud veteran, I often return to my military training as a beacon of light. In the United States Army, there is a foundational truth taught to every soldier from day one: you do not choose the terrain you fight on, and you do not win a campaign with a divided platoon. You win through discipline, unity of command, and a leader who never leaves a soldier behind. From the streets of Crown Heights to the floor of the House, Jeffries has stood shoulder-to-shoulder with every wing of our Caucus— Members in purple districts, staunch progressives, members of the Congressional Asian and Pacific American Caucus, Black Caucus, Hispanic Caucus, and Equality Caucus, veterans, and newcomers alike. He listens to his Members, builds a unified battle plan, and ensures that when we march onto the House floor, we move as one cohesive unit. He has fearlessly led our party through the dark days of the Trump administration, advocated on behalf of American families, and will chart a new path forward for Democrats to deliver prosperity to the American people. He came to Congress as a freshman Member from Brooklyn, rose to leadership and became the first African American to serve as a party leader in Congress, and now Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries will make history as the first Black Speaker of the House of Representatives. I have full faith that he will meet this responsibility with the expertise and devotion that this moment requires. I look forward to working with my dear friends, Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries, our new House Majority Leader Katherine Clark, Majority Whip Pete Aguilar, Assistant Speaker Joe Neguse, Caucus Chair Ted Lieu, and Caucus Vice Chair Lauren Underwood to meet the needs of Orange and LA counties, lower costs for Americans nationwide, protect the rights and benefits of our veterans, and serve our country with pride.” ### Issues : Congress Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) celebrated the passage of the Major Richard Star Act, which will allow combat-injured veterans to receive their full retirement pay and disability compensation simultaneously. Representative Tran co-sponsored the bill and signed the discharge petition to bring the bill to the House Floor, where it passed shortly after Veterans Day. Unlike past legislation, this bill also applies to veterans with a combat-related disability who have fewer than 20 years of service, expanding access to VA benefits. Now, the bill awaits Senate consideration. Under the current policy, service members are required to return home and retire from service upon being injured. During retirement, their earned disability benefits are deducted from their retirement benefits, significantly decreasing their monthly compensation – which covers their food, medicine, and other critical expenses. If passed by the Senate, this legislation would allow all combat-injured veterans who were medically retired, regardless of the length of their service, to accept the full amount of their earned disability and retirement benefits. “As an Army veteran, my commitment to my brothers and sisters who served is steadfast. Under current policy, combat-injured veterans are forced to forfeit part of their benefits because of injuries beyond their control. It’s just plain wrong: combat-injured veterans must receive their full disability and retirement pay, full stop. I’m proud to have supported this bill to expand benefits for those who sustained lasting injuries in service to our country, and I urge my Senate colleagues to swiftly pass this bipartisan legislation,” said Representative Tran. H.R. 2102 , or the Major Richard Star Act, was introduced by Representative Gus Bilirakis (R-FL-12); however, at the time, it was not considered by the House Armed Services Committee. Representative Mark Takano (D-CA-39) brought the bill to the House Floor through a discharge petition , which garnered the required 218 signatures needed to be considered on the House floor. On Thursday, November 12, 2026, the bill passed 392-18. This legislation was named after the late Major Richard Star of the U.S. Army Reserve, a combat-injured veteran and advocate for injured veterans. As a member of the powerful House Armed Services Committee, Representative Tran is continuously working to expand protections and benefits for veterans: In July 2025 , Representative Tran led a letter with Representative Correa to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), urging federal support for the construction of the Southern California Veterans Cemetery at Gypsum Canyon. In September 2026 , Representative Tran and colleagues sent a letter to Governor Gavin Newsom to ensure CalVets accepts the funding to build the cemetery. Rep. Tran’s first piece of legislation, the Protect Veteran Jobs Act , supports the livelihoods of veterans who were wrongfully removed from their civil service positions and allows them to continue serving their country as part of the federal workforce. Representative Tran introduced the bipartisan Delivering Digitally to Our Veterans Act to allow veterans the option to receive G.I. Bill information and benefits through electronic messages, reducing unnecessary paperwork and increasing accessibility. Representative Tran also introduced the Carlton H. Ingram Veterans’ Benefits Protection Act to protect veterans’ disability benefits from a change at the Department of Veterans Affairs that would have cut benefits for veterans who rely on medication to manage their disabilities. ### Issues : Veterans Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) led a letter urging the Senate to act on 32 House-passed bills that would help the nation's 36.2 million small businesses, including over 400,000 small businesses in Orange County. Out of the bills listed in the letter, Rep. Tran personally shepherded the following: Introducing H.R. 5788 - the 504 Program Risk Oversight Act, which would increase transparency and efficiency within the Small Business Administration, Co-Leading H.R. 787 - the Plain Language in Contracting Act, which would help small businesses compete for government contracts, and Co-Leading H.R. 1642 - the Connecting Small Businesses with Career and Technical Education Graduates Act, which would connect small businesses with a more robust workforce pipeline. Alongside Rep. Tran, this bipartisan letter was co-led by Representatives Kimberlyn King-Hinds (R-MP-AL), Johnny Olszewski, Jr. (D-MD-02), and Tony Wied (R-WI-08), and signed by additional members of the House Small Business Committee, including Representatives Lateefah Simon (D-CA-12), Gilbert Ray Cisneros, Jr. (D-CA-31), Kelly Morrison (D-MN-03), Pete Stauber (R-MN-08), and Hillary J. Scholten (D-MI-03). Currently, over 30 bipartisan small business bills have passed the House of Representatives and are awaiting Senate consideration. This includes legislation that would expand workforce development, address fraud, improve transparency, and enhance technology solutions for small businesses across the nation. In the letter to Chairwoman Ernst and Ranking Member Markey of the Senate Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship (Senate SBC), Rep. Tran and his colleagues called on their Senate counterpart committee to prioritize the passage of this legislation before the 119th Congress ends in January. If the Senate fails to act before the end of the 119th Congress, all 32 bipartisan bills will expire. Each bill would have to be reintroduced in the 120th Congress and restart the legislative process, further delaying relief for American small businesses. “As Members of the House Small Business Committee, we urge the Senate Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship (Senate SBC) to prioritize consideration of bipartisan small business legislation that has already passed the House of Representatives. Congress must take every opportunity to advance policies that strengthen small businesses’ ability to invest, innovate, create jobs, and serve their communities. With limited time remaining in the 119th Congress, we respectfully urge that the Senate SBC act on them before the end of this year,” the members wrote in the letter. “As a second-generation small business owner, I know what it takes to operate a family-owned business. Californians need legislation that makes it easier, not harder, to successfully pursue entrepreneurship. As members of the House Small Business Committee, we have proudly passed thirty-two bipartisan, common-sense bills that will help small business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs throughout California and the country. The 119th Congress is quickly coming to a close, and the Senate must do its part and consider these bills before time is up,” said Representative Tran . “Members of the House Small Business Committee have been hard at work this Congress passing legislation to support our small businesses and put Main Street first,” said Congressman Wied. “Legislation like H.R. 4549 and H.R. 8879, which I was proud to co-lead, are exactly the types of bills small business owners deserve, helping increase transparency and ensuring rural small businesses have access to the tools they need to succeed. It’s time for the Senate to take action and get these important bills across the finish line.” “Small businesses are the backbone of our communities, and they need access to the resources to grow and succeed. The House has passed more than 30 bipartisan bills, including my Northern Mariana Islands Small Business Access Act, which would make CNMI small businesses eligible for SBA microloans, helping entrepreneurs access the capital they need to start and grow their businesses. Now it’s time for the Senate to act and get these bills across the finish line,” said Congresswoman Kimberlyn King-Hinds (MP-AL). “Small business owners don't have time to wait on Washington: they need a government that works as hard as they do and policies that help them grow, hire, and compete," said Congressman Johnny Olszewski. "The House has done its work, passing more than 30 bipartisan bills that deliver practical solutions for Main Street America. Now it's time for the Senate to step up and get these bills across the finish line before this term expires.” Read the full letter and the full summary of legislation HERE . ### Issues : Economy & Small Business Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; San Pedro, CA – On Tuesday, October 27, Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) alongside Ways and Means Trade Subcommittee Ranking Member Linda Sánchez (CA-38), Rep. Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28), Rep. Jimmy Gomez (CA-34), Rep. Sydney Kam la ger-Dove (CA-37), Rep. Ted Lieu (CA-36), and Rep. George Whitesides (CA-27) convened at the Port of Los Angeles for a roundtable discussion on the impact of President Trump’s trade policies on the port and California’s statewide and local economy. The members heard from port officials, union members, business leaders, and other stakeholders about the damage caused by President Trump’s trade policies. His tariffs cost the average American household over $1,000 la st year, while creating uncertainty for businesses, hurting farmers and ex port ers, and disrupting cargo at the port that sup port s 126,000 jobs in LA and 1.3 million jobs throughout the U.S. The Port of Los Angeles is the nation’s busiest container port , handling more than 10 million containers a year. Together with the Port of Long Beach, the two port s move about 31 percent of the nation’s container trade. The port is run by the City of Los Angeles and covers 7,500 acres of la nd and water, with 43 miles of waterfront, 25 cargo terminals, 85 container cranes and 122 miles of on-dock rail. “President Trump’s reckless tariffs are directly impacting the Port of Los Angeles and the critical cargo that moves through its waters,” said Congressman Tran. “As our nation’s busiest container port , the economic impact of higher costs and trade uncertainty is felt throughout our state and our country, hurting California’s trade-reliant industries, la bor force, and everyday consumers. I’m grateful that Congresswoman Sanchez convened myself, my colleagues, and stakeholders to learn more about this trade crisis. As co-chair of the Lowering Costs Caucus, I will continue to speak out against this Administration’s poor economic policies that harm the families and businesses in my district.” “It’s clear that President Trump’s chaotic trade policies are hurting Americans,” said Ranking Member Sánchez, the top Democrat on the Trade Subcommittee. “Families are paying more for everyday goods. Small businesses can’t p la n from one month to the next. Farmers are losing access to overseas markets. And the workers who keep the nation’s busiest port running are left wondering what comes next. Southern California’s workers and families deserve better, and so does the rest of the country.” “We heard directly from the businesses, truckers, farmers, and workers paying the price for the Trump administration’s reckless economic policies,” said Congresswoman Barragán. “Between skyrocketing fuel costs from Trump’s war on Iran and his constantly changing tariffs, businesses are struggling, truckers are being squeezed, and working families are footing the bill. The Port of Los Angeles is an economic engine for the entire country, and we must end these harmful tariff taxes, restore stability to our supply chains, and lower costs for American families.” “President Trump promised his tariffs would revive American manufacturing and boost ex port s. But as we heard firsthand at the Port of Los Angeles, his chaotic trade policies are undermining American businesses, disrupting supply chains, and leaving working families to foot the bill,” said Congresswoman Chu. “Families are paying more for everyday essentials, while businesses are still waiting for refunds on tariffs the Supreme Court struck down. That’s unacceptable. As a member of the Ways and Means Committee, I’ll keep fighting to lower costs, ensure businesses receive the refunds they’re owed, and advance trade policies that sup port American workers and grow our economy. I thank Congresswoman Sánchez for bringing us together to hear directly from those impacted by these policies.” “The Port of Los Angeles is the backbone of our national supply chain and the lifeblood of working families across CA-37,” said Congresswoman Kam la ger-Dove. “But Trump’s temper tariffs have injected chaos into port operations, burdened small businesses, and driven up costs by $1,000 a year for consumers already struggling to make ends meet. I was proud to join Rep. Sánchez and colleagues to hear directly from port stakeholders about how erratic trade policies are hurting our nation’s busiest port and entire economy. As a member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, I’ll keep fighting to strengthen the Port of LA , support the workers who keep goods moving, and ensure our region remains a leader in the global economy.” “The Port of Los Angeles is the la rgest container port in the United States, bringing essential goods to American businesses and consumers while connecting California businesses with markets around the world,” said Congressman Lieu. “But the Trump administration’s reckless tariffs and chaotic trade policies are driving up costs and putting businesses at risk. I’m grateful to Congresswoman Sánchez for organizing this event and for port leadership, la bor leadership, and industry stakeholders for bringing attention to these challenges. I will continue fighting to protect California’s businesses and the workers and communities that depend on them.” “All across Los Angeles County, businesses and entire industries have been devastated by rising costs caused by the administration’s tariffs,” said Congressman Whitesides. “I’m grateful to have had the chance to join Reps. Sanchez, Barragán, and other colleagues to speak directly with Port of LA officials and other stakeholders to talk about the issues they are facing and how we can ensure California’s economy stays strong even in the midst of harmful federal actions. I’ll keep pushing to reverse the administration’s erratic trade policies that force the American consumer to pay the price.” Congressman Tran led a letter with his National Security Task Force co-chairs Representatives Jason Crow (CO-06) and Maggie Good la nder (NH-02) to President Trump and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth demanding a full public accounting of the economic costs of the war with Iran as prices rise for American families nationwide. Additionally, Representatives Derek Tran, Hil la ry Scholten (MI-03), and Greg La ndsman (OH-01), co-chairs of the Lowering Costs Caucus, introduced legis la tion to assess the impacts of President Trump’s trade policies on the cost of goods for everyday American families. Tran introduced the Baby Food Tax Relief Act to exempt essential baby food products – including high chairs, bottles, and formu la —from President Trump’s tariffs. Congressman Tran, alongside other House Democrats signed onto a discharge petition to quash Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs, which would have ended the President’s tariff policy that has increased costs for American businesses. ### Issues : Economy & Small Business Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Washington, D.C. – During last month’s United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) sent a letter to the U.S. Department of State demanding the U.S. government hold the communist Vietnamese government accountable for widespread human rights abuses. In a recent response, the Department of State affirmed its concerns about Vietnam’s human rights record and confirmed that these issues were discussed in a conversation between Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor, Riley Barnes, and Vietnam’s Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dang Hoang Giang. “As the United States Mission to the United Nations interacts with the delegation from the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, including Party General Secretary and State President Tô Lâm, I urge you to discuss human rights, call for the release of prisoners of conscience, raise concern about parts of the Penal Code that criminalize peaceful dissent, and affirm that stronger relations with Vietnam must be accompanied by measurable and verifiable progress on human rights,” said Representative Tran in the letter. Read Representative Tran’s letter HERE . “During the UNGA meetings, Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor Riley Barnes expressed his concerns to Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs Dang Hoang Giang on September 22, where he called for the release of unjustly detained political prisoners, including Le Huu Minh Tuan, and discussed transnational repression affecting U.S. citizens, freedom of expression, and religious freedom,” Katherine Bowles, Assistant Secretary, Bureau of Legislative Affairs, wrote in response. Read the Department of State’s response HERE . Representative Tran remains steadfast in demanding accountability for the Vietnamese government’s anti-democratic practices and human rights violations. As the son of Vietnamese refugees and the only Vietnamese American in Congress, Representative Tran is committed to uplifting and representing the Vietnamese community on the national stage and protecting the rights of immigrants. In an April 2026 letter to General Secretary Tô Lâm, Congressman Tran demanded a visit with prisoners of conscience imprisoned by the Socialist Republic of Vietnam to monitor their well-being. In April 2025, during the 50th commemoration of the Fall of Saigon , Congressman Tran held a roundtable with Vietnamese human rights activists and former prisoners of conscience to uplift their firsthand accounts of the oppression they faced at the hands of the Vietnamese government. Additionally, Tran introduced a congressional resolution to formally mark April 30, 2026 as the 51st anniversary of Black April. Tran, a vocal advocate for advancing human rights in Vietnam, co-led H.R. 3122, the bipartisan Vietnam Human Rights Act, to hold Vietnamese communist officials accountable for human rights abuses and establish human rights and fair-trade priorities for U.S.-Vietnam relations. Congressman Tran serves as the official sponsor of Le Huu Minh Tuan, a Vietnamese journalist who was wrongfully imprisoned by the communist government, through the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission’s Defending Freedoms Project and continues to fight for the release of prisoners of conscience around the world. In March 2025 , Congressman Tran sent a letter to Secretary of State Rubio requesting their immediate assistance to secure the release of Le Huu Minh Tuan. ### Issues : Human Rights Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) led a letter with Democratic colleagues to Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Markwayne Mullin and Acting Director of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) David Venturella, demanding answers on the detention and deportation of “Amerasians,” or individuals born in Asia to an Asian mother and U.S. serviceman during the Southeast Asia War between 1950 and 1982. Under the Amerasian Act of 1982 and the Amerasian Homecoming Act of 1988, many were able to gain Lawful Permanent Residency status in the United States. However, because they were not categorically naturalized and many do not have proper documentation of American paternity, Amerasians are now facing threats of deportation. “It has been extremely difficult for Amerasians to verify their ancestry. Most of their fathers returned to the U.S. after their tours of duty. Many of their mothers destroyed documents to protect their children in fear of political retaliation and persecution,” said Rep. Tran in the letter. In 2008, the United States and Vietnam signed a memorandum agreeing to halt the repatriation of Southeast Asian refugees who arrived in the U.S. prior to 1995. This agreement was heavily altered in November 2020, allowing a process for deporting immigrants who entered the U.S. before 1995. Protections were rolled back even more in June 2025, leaving an unknown number of Amerasians vulnerable to detention and deportation. The letter was signed by Chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus, Representative Grace Meng (NY-06), and Representatives Lou Correa (CA-46), Judy Chu (CA-28), Dave Min (CA-47), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Raja Krishamoorthi (IL-08), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Juan Vargas (CA-52), and Seth Moulton (MA-06). Read the full letter HERE . Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) and members of the California Congressional delegation conducted an unannounced oversight visit to Adelanto ICE Processing Center in Adelanto, California. Alongside Rep. Tran, members of the visiting delegation included Ranking Member of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, Representative Robert Garcia (CA-42), and Representatives Judy Chu (CA-28), Dave Min (CA-47), Norma Torres (CA-35), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), and Luz Rivas (CA-29). The group toured the facility, where they observed the conditions where detainees are being held. They were not permitted to speak directly with the detained individuals. “Adelanto has a troubling history of denying detainees proper medical care, allowing unsafe conditions, and refusing to take responsibility for the harrowing deaths that have occurred in its facilities,” said Representative Tran. “We came here to carry out our constitutional responsibilities as Members of Congress: conduct oversight, enforce accountability, and protect our communities. As the son of Vietnamese refugees, this is personal to me — and it’s personal to the hardworking immigrants in my district, too. I will not rest until the Trump Administration answers for the deaths and mistreatment that have taken place at Adelanto, and across the country.” Federal law guarantees Members of Congress access to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) detention facilities for oversight purposes. Representative Tran previously visited Adelanto ICE Processing Center in June 2025, where he was denied entry, alongside Representatives Gil Cisneros (CA-31) and Judy Chu (CA-28). Days later, he joined Reps. Cisneros and Chu in a letter to then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and then-Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons condemning the agencies for unlawfully denying them entry to the facility. Representative Tran introduced the Private Detention and Corporate Accountability Act to hold privately owned detention centers that contract with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) accountable for wrongful deaths that occur in their facilities or under their care. This legislation would also apply to the Adelanto ICE Processing Center. Tran also co-led the ICE and CBP Constitutional Accountability Act to provide a path to justice for victims of ICE’s constitutional rights abuses. Tran has voted against H.R. 7147, the Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act of 2026, which provides more funding for ICE without requiring basic guardrails to keep U.S. citizens from being detained or deported. Tran has also cosponsored the following legislation to curtail ICE’s reckless behavior, increase transparency within ICE-related operations, and affirm the rights of immigrants that are detained by DHS: H.R. 4176, The No Secret Police Act , to prohibit ICE agents from wearing non-tactical face coverings while on duty; H.R. 5973, The Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act , to limit the use of force during immigration operations; H.R. 3172, The ICE Visibility Act , to require agents to clearly identify themselves as Customs and Border Protection officers when interacting with the public; H.R. 5653, The Trust Through Transparency Act , to require all ICE officials to wear body cameras when publicly carrying out immigration enforcement operations; H.R. 944, The Access to Counsel Act , to ensure that U.S. citizens and individuals with lawful status can contact an attorney or family member to seek legal assistance when they are detained; H.R. 5941, The Restoring Access for Detainees Act , to require DHS to allow noncitizens who have been detained to contact their legal counsel and families; and H.R. 4456, Stop ICE from Kidnapping U.S. Citizens Act , to prohibit ICE from using federal funds to detain or deport U.S. citizens. ### Issues : Immigration Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Condado de Orange, California – El representante Derek Tran (CA-45) ha emitido la siguiente declaración en respuesta al anuncio de la Fiscalía del Condado de Orange de que ha alcanzado un acuerdo de 125 millones de dólares con GKN Aerospace tras la emergencia relacionada con un depósito de sustancias químicas tóxicas en mayo de 2026, que provocó la evacuación de 50000 residentes y negocios: “Me tranquiliza ver que el Condado de Orange y GKN han llegado a un acuerdo que da prioridad a las necesidades de los residentes y los propietarios de pequeñas empresas que se vieron afectados por la evacuación forzosa de mayo”, dijo el representante Tran. “Espero que este acuerdo pueda superar rápidamente el proceso de aprobación judicial, para que podamos poner en marcha el proceso de reclamaciones y gestionar la ayuda económica y los reembolsos que tanto necesitan los afectados. Seguiré vigilando de cerca la situación para garantizar que las familias, las empresas y los socios comunitarios reciban una indemnización adecuada.’’ “Todos los californianos merecen sentirse seguros en su propio hogar, sin temor a ser desalojados ni a sufrir trastornos. Como su representante en el Congreso, supervisaré de primera mano la aplicación del plan de seguridad integral de GKN a medida que avancen en sus operaciones de fabricación.” El acuerdo extrajudicial, presentado por la Fiscalía del Condado de Orange el lunes 12 de octubre, está pendiente de aprobación por parte del Tribunal Superior del Condado de Orange. En respuesta a la evacuación de mayo de 2026, el representante Tran presentó la Ley de Transparencia sobre Materiales Peligrosos , que obligaría a instalaciones como GKN a informar adecuadamente a las comunidades en las que operan sobre las medidas de seguridad establecidas para proteger a los residentes y a las pequeñas empresas. ### Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; WASHINGTON, D.C. – El representante Derek Tran (CA-45) ha presentado la Ley de Ayuda al Coste de la Vivienda para Inquilinos (COST), con el fin de ofrecer alivio a los inquilinos del sur de California que se enfrentan al aumento de los costes de la vivienda. La legislación establece créditos fiscales integrales para los inquilinos, lo que contribuye al compromiso constante del representante Tran de ampliar la asequibilidad de la vivienda. "Los costos de la vivienda en todo el país, especialmente en el sur de California, han llegado a un punto crítico. Las familias apenas pueden pagar la renta, y mucho menos ahorrar para el futuro", afirmó el representante Tran. "Este proyecto de ley proporcionaría un alivio inmediato y tangible a los inquilinos necesitados, ayudándoles a mantener un techo sobre sus cabezas, a disponer de más margen en sus presupuestos para los gastos diarios o incluso a ahorrar para comprar una casa. Me enorgullece estar al frente de esta iniciativa en representación de todas las familias estadounidenses." Las familias del sur de California se enfrentan a unos de los costes de vivienda más elevados del país, con un alquiler medio en el condado de Orange que supera los 3.200 dólares al mes y que se ha disparado casi un 40% desde 2017. La propuesta legislativa introduce un nuevo crédito fiscal reembolsable básico del 8 % para las familias con unos ingresos brutos de 150 000 dólares o menos, con un límite máximo por hogar de 333 dólares al mes, lo que supone un total de 4 000 dólares al año. En el distrito 45 de California, esto beneficiaría a más de 75 000 hogares. Mientras que otras medidas para reducir los costos de la vivienda tardarían tiempo en aplicarse, este proyecto de ley devuelve inmediatamente dinero a los inquilinos para que puedan hacer frente a los gastos de alimentación, medicamentos, cuidado de los hijos y otros gastos. Esta iniciativa legislativa se suma al historial del representante Tran en la consecución de resultados en materia de vivienda para la región: El representante Tran consiguió 250 000 dólares en financiación federal para apoyar la construcción de 2700 viviendas permanentes asequibles en todo el condado de Orange. El representante Tran copatrocinó la Ley Saving the American Dream (Salvar el sueño americano) para crear un grupo de trabajo interinstitucional sobre la crisis de la vivienda, así como la Ley de Mejora de los Créditos para la Vivienda Asequible , destinada a financiar la construcción de más viviendas multifamiliares. Además, el representante Tran votó a favor de la Ley "21st Century ROAD to Housing", que entró en vigor en julio de 2026 y tiene por objeto acelerar la construcción de viviendas y reducir los trámites burocráticos. ORANGE COUNTY, California – Dân Biểu Liên Bang Derek Trần (CA-45) đưa ra tuyên bố sau khi Biện Lý Cuộc Orange County thông báo đạt được thỏa thuận bồi thường trị giá $125 triệu với công ty GKN Aerospace, liên quan đến sự việc bồn chứa hóa chất độc hại hồi Tháng Năm, 2026, khiến 50,000 cư dân và cơ sở kinh doanh phải di tản. “Tôi cảm thấy nhẹ nhõm khi Orange County và GKN đạt được thỏa thuận đặt quyền lợi của người dân và các chủ doanh nghiệp nhỏ bị ảnh hưởng do lệnh di tản bắt buộc hồi Tháng Năm lên hàng đầu,” Dân Biểu Derek Trần cho biết. “Tôi hy vọng thỏa thuận này sẽ sớm được tòa phê chuẩn để có thể bắt đầu tiếp nhận hồ sơ yêu cầu bồi thường, đồng thời nhanh chóng cung cấp khoản hỗ trợ tài chính và hoàn trả các chi phí cần thiết cho những người bị ảnh hưởng. Tôi sẽ tiếp tục theo dõi sát sao tình hình để bảo đảm các gia đình, doanh nghiệp và tổ chức cộng đồng được bồi thường thỏa đáng.” “Mọi người dân California đều xứng đáng được sống an toàn trong chính ngôi nhà của mình, không phải lo sợ bị buộc di dời hay xáo trộn cuộc sống. Với vai trò là dân biểu đại diện quý vị tại Quốc Hội, tôi sẽ giám sát chặt chẽ việc GKN thực hiện đầy đủ kế hoạch an toàn toàn diện trong quá trình tiếp tục hoạt động sản xuất.” Thỏa thuận bồi thường được Biện Lý Cuộc Orange County đệ trình lên tòa hôm Thứ Hai, ngày 12 Tháng Mười, và hiện đang chờ Tòa Thượng Thẩm Orange County phê chuẩn. Sau vụ di tản hồi Tháng Năm, Dân Biểu Derek Trần đệ trình Dự Luật Minh Bạch Thông Tin Về Vật Liệu Nguy Hiểm (Hazardous Materials Transparency Act ) nhằm yêu cầu các cơ sở như GKN phải thông báo đầy đủ cho cộng đồng nơi họ hoạt động về những biện pháp an toàn được áp dụng để bảo vệ cư dân và các doanh nghiệp nhỏ. ### Issues : Public Safety Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Orange County, CA – Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) released the following statement in response to an announcement from the Orange County District Attorney's Office that it has reached a $125 million settlement agreement with GKN Aerospace following the toxic chemical tank emergency in May 2026 that resulted in the evacuation of 50,000 residents and businesses: “I’m relieved to see that Orange County and GKN have reached an agreement that prioritizes the needs of the residents and small business owners who were affected by the forced evacuation in May,” said Representative Tran. “I hope this settlement can move through the court approval process swiftly, so we can launch the claims process and administer much-needed financial assistance and reimbursement to those affected. I will continue to monitor the situation closely to ensure the families, businesses, and community partners are appropriately compensated.” “Every Californian deserves to feel safe in their own home without fear of displacement or disruption. As your Member of Congress, I will closely monitor the enforcement of GKN’s comprehensive safety plan, as they move forward in their manufacturing operations.” The settlement agreement, filed by the Orange County District Attorney's Office on Monday, October 12, is pending approval from the Orange County Superior Court. In response to the May 2026 evacuation, Representative Tran introduced the Hazardous Materials Transparency Act , which would require facilities like GKN to adequately notify the communities in which they operate about the safety measures in place to protect residents and small businesses. ### Issues : Public Safety Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; WASHINGTON, DC – Dân Biểu Liên Bang Derek Trần (CA-45) giới thiệu Dự Luật Hỗ Trợ Chi Phí Sinh Hoạt Nhà Ở cho Người Thuê Nhà (COST) Act, để hỗ trợ cư dân tại Nam California đang phải đối mặt với chi phí nhà ở ngày càng tăng. Dự luật thiết lập các khoản tín dụng thuế dành cho người thuê nhà, tiếp nối nỗ lực của Dân Biểu Derek nhằm giúp người dân có thêm cơ hội tiếp cận nhà ở với chi phí hợp lý. “Chi phí nhà ở trên cả nước, đặc biệt tại Nam California, đã tăng đến mức báo động. Nhiều gia đình phải chật vật mới đủ tiền trả tiền thuê nhà, chưa nói đến việc tiết kiệm cho tương lai,” Dân Biểu Derek Trần cho biết. “Dự luật này sẽ mang lại sự hỗ trợ thiết thực và kịp thời cho những người thuê nhà đang gặp khó khăn, giúp họ trang trải tiền thuê nhà, có thêm ngân sách cho các chi phí sinh hoạt hằng ngày, hoặc thậm chí dành dụm để mua nhà. Tôi tự hào dẫn đầu nỗ lực này vì các gia đình khắp nước Mỹ.” Các gia đình tại Nam California phải đối mặt với mức chi phí nhà ở thuộc hàng cao nhất cả nước. Tại Orange County, tiền thuê nhà trung bình hiện vượt $3,200 mỗi tháng , tăng gần 40% kể từ năm 2017 . Dự luật đề nghị một khoản tín dụng thuế hoàn lại ở mức căn bản 8% dành cho các gia đình có tổng thu nhập từ $150,000 trở xuống, với mức hỗ trợ tối đa $333 mỗi tháng cho mỗi gia đình, tương đương $4,000 mỗi năm. Riêng tại Địa Hạt 45 của California, hơn 75,000 gia đình có thể được hưởng lợi từ chính sách này. Trong khi những giải pháp khác nhằm giảm chi phí nhà ở có thể cần nhiều thời gian để thực hiện, dự luật này sẽ trực tiếp giúp người thuê nhà có thêm tiền để trang trải thực phẩm, thuốc men, chi phí chăm sóc trẻ em, và các nhu cầu thiết yếu khác. Nỗ lực lập pháp này tiếp nối những hoạt động của Dân Biểu Derek Trần nhằm giải quyết vấn đề nhà ở trong khu vực: Dân Biểu Derek Trần đã vận động thành công $250,000 ngân sách liên bang để hỗ trợ xây dựng 2,700 căn nhà ở giá phải chăng lâu dài khắp Orange County. Dân Biểu Derek đồng bảo trợ Dự Luật Saving the American Dream Act , nhằm thành lập một lực lượng đặc nhiệm liên cơ quan để giải quyết cuộc khủng hoảng nhà ở, và Dự Luật Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act , hỗ trợ tài chính cho việc xây dựng thêm các khu nhà ở nhiều căn. Ngoài ra, Dân Biểu Derek đã bỏ phiếu ủng hộ Dự Luật 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act , được ký thành luật vào Tháng Bảy, 2026, đẩy nhanh tiến độ xây dựng nhà ở và giảm bớt các thủ tục hành chính không cần thiết. WASHINGTON, DC – Dân Biểu Liên Bang Derek Trần (CA-45) đồng bảo trợ H.R.1314 , Dự Luật Bảo Vệ và Hỗ Trợ Thu Nhập Từ Tiền Tip (TIPS Act), cho phép người lao động trong ngành dịch vụ được khấu trừ tiền tip khi khai thuế. Dự luật sẽ nâng mức thu nhập gộp điều chỉnh tối đa để người lao động ngành dịch vụ đủ điều kiện hưởng khoản khấu trừ này từ $25,000 lên $112,500, đồng thời áp dụng thay đổi này lâu dài cho người lao động ngành dịch vụ khắp toàn quốc. “Trong lúc giá cả tăng vọt do cuộc chiến thiếu thận trọng của Tổng Thống Trump tại Iran và các chính sách thuế quan thiếu trách nhiệm, các gia đình lao động đang phải chịu áp lực rất lớn khi chật vật trang trải cuộc sống. Đối với người lao động ngành dịch vụ, tiền tip là nguồn thu nhập thiết yếu để lo bữa ăn, chi trả các khoản sinh hoạt hằng ngày và chăm lo cho gia đình. Tôi tự hào đồng bảo trợ Dự Luật TIPS vì sẽ mang lại lợi ích kinh tế thiết thực cho người lao động ngành dịch vụ và gia đình họ tại Nam California – giúp họ giữ lại nhiều tiền hơn và giúp họ ổn định tài chính lâu dài,” Dân Biểu Derek Trần cho biết. Dự Luật TIPS áp dụng cho người lao động trong các ngành thẩm mỹ, khách sạn, ăn uống, dịch vụ đậu xe và vệ sinh, qua đó mang lại lợi ích cho gần 70,000 người lao động ngành dịch vụ tại Địa Hạt 45 của California. Dự luật được Dân Biểu Steven Horsford (NV-04) giới thiệu tại Quốc Hội khóa 119. Khác với điều khoản trong H.R. 1 – còn được gọi là “One Big Beautiful Bill Act” – dự luật này sẽ duy trì lâu dài mức khấu trừ thuế cao hơn dành cho người lao động ngành dịch vụ, thay vì để chính sách hết hiệu lực vào cuối năm 2028. Dân Biểu Derek Trần tiếp tục tập trung giải quyết cuộc khủng hoảng chi phí sinh hoạt và không ngừng ủng hộ các dự luật nhằm giảm chi phí cho các gia đình lao động: Vào Tháng Năm, 2026, Dân Biểu Derek cùng các thành viên của Lowering Costs Caucus gửi thư kêu gọi chính quyền Tổng Thống Trump có biện pháp giải quyết tình trạng giá năng lượng tăng vọt. Vào Tháng Bảy, 2025, Dân Biểu Derek giới thiệu Dự Luật Giảm Thuế Thực Phẩm Trẻ Em , nhằm miễn thuế quan đối với các sản phẩm thiết yếu phục vụ việc nuôi trẻ nhỏ, như sữa công thức, ghế ăn cho trẻ em và bình sữa, qua đó giúp giảm chi phí cho các bậc phụ huynh lao động. Dân Biểu Derek cũng đồng bảo trợ Dự Luật Cải Thiện Tín Dụng Nhà Ở Giá Phải Chăng , nhằm hỗ trợ tài chính cho việc xây dựng thêm nhà ở nhiều căn, và Dự Luật Tín Dụng Thuế Cho Người Mua Nhà Lần Đầu , thiết lập khoản tín dụng thuế có thể hoàn lại dành cho người mua nhà lần đầu. ### Issues : Economy & Small Business Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) joined Rep. Lou Correa and a bipartisan group of lawmakers this week to send a letter urging Governor Gavin Newsom to ensure the California Department of Veterans Affairs (CalVet) accepts $10 million in federal funding offered by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) for the Southern California Veterans Cemetery at Gypsum Canyon. Representatives Lou Correa, Ken Calvert, Young Kim, Mike Levin, and Dave Min, alongside State Senator Thomas J. Umberg and Assemblymembers Sharon Quirk-Silva and Avelino Valencia, joined Tran in signing the letter. “After more than a decade of work, we are closer than ever to fulfilling our promise to Orange County’s veterans and their families,” said the lawmakers. “We should not allow $10 million in federal funding secured for this purpose to be left on the table.” Read the full letter HERE . On July 27, 2021, the Orange County Board of Supervisors approved $20 million for site development for a veterans’ cemetery at Gypsum Canyon, designating more than 200 acres of county-owned land near the 91 Freeway and 241 Toll Road for a public cemetery and a separate veterans’ cemetery. Combined state and local funding for the veterans’ cemetery construction now totals $50 million, including $25 million from prior state budgets and an additional $5 million allocated in the 2024 State Budget Act. The funding allocated has yet to be accepted by the California Department of Veterans Affairs. An Army veteran and a member of the powerful House Armed Services Committee, Representative Tran is dedicated to expanding protections and benefits for veterans: In July 2025 , Representative Tran led a letter with Representative Correa to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), urging federal support for the construction of the Southern California Veterans Cemetery at Gypsum Canyon. Rep. Tran’s first piece of legislation, the Protect Veteran Jobs Act , supports the livelihoods of veterans who were wrongfully removed from their civil service positions and allows them to continue serving their country as part of the federal workforce. Representative Tran introduced the bipartisan Delivering Digitally to Our Veterans Act to allow veterans the option to receive G.I. Bill information and benefits through electronic messages, reducing unnecessary paperwork and increasing accessibility. Representative Tran also introduced the Carlton H. Ingram Veterans’ Benefits Protection Act to protect veterans’ disability benefits from a change at the Department of Veterans Affairs that would have cut benefits for veterans who rely on medication to manage their disabilities. ### Issues : Veterans Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) introduced the Housing Cost of Living Support for Tenants (COST) Act, to deliver relief to Southern California renters struggling with rising housing costs. The legislation creates comprehensive tax credits for renters, contributing to Representative Tran’s ongoing commitment to expand housing affordability. “Housing costs across the country, especially in Southern California have reached a breaking point. Families are barely scraping by to pay rent, let alone save for the future,” said Representative Tran. “This bill would provide immediate, tangible relief to renters in need, helping them keep a roof over their heads, provide more room in their budgets for everyday expenses, or even save to buy a home. I am proud to lead this effort on behalf of all American families.” Southern California families face some of the highest housing costs in the nation, with the average rent in Orange County being over $3,200 a month and skyrocketing almost 40% , since 2017. The proposed legislation introduces a new, baseline 8% refundable tax credit for families who make a gross income of $150,000 or less, with a maximum household cap of $333 a month, totaling $4,000 a year. In California’s 45th Congressional District, this would benefit over 75,000 households. While other efforts to lower housing costs would take time to implement, this bill immediately puts money back in the hands of renters as they tackle the costs of groceries, medication, childcare, and other expenses. This legislative push builds on Representative Tran’s record of delivering housing results for the region: Rep. Tran secured $250,000 in federal funding to support the construction of 2,700 permanent affordable housing units across Orange County. Tran cosponsored the Saving the American Dream Act to create an interagency task force on the housing crisis and the Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act to finance the building of more multifamily units. Additionally, Rep. Tran voted for the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which became law in July 2026 and works to speed up homebuilding and reduce regulatory red tape. Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) co-sponsored H.R. 1314 , the Tipped Income Protection and Support Act (TIPS Act) to allow service industry professionals to deduct their tips when filing taxes. This legislation would increase the maximum amount that service workers can deduct from an adjusted gross income of $25,000 to $112,500, and make this change permanent for service workers across the country. “While prices skyrocket due to President Trump’s reckless war in Iran and irresponsible tariff policies, working families are under an immense amount of stress as they struggle to make ends meet. For service workers, tips are essential to putting food on the table, handling everyday expenses, and providing for their loved ones. I’m a proud cosponsor of the TIPS Act because it creates a measurable economic impact for service workers and their families in Southern California — putting more money in their pockets and strengthening their financial futures,” said Representative Tran . The TIPS Act applies to cosmetology, hospitality, food/beverage, parking, and custodial service employees, benefiting nearly 70,000 service industry professionals in California’s 45th Congressional District. This legislation was introduced by Representative Steven Horsford (NV-04) in the 119th Congress. Unlike the provision in H.R.1 – the so-called “One Big Beautiful Bill Act” – this legislation would make the increased deduction for service workers permanent instead of sunsetting it at the end of 2028. Representative Tran remains focused on addressing the affordability crisis and has continuously championed legislation to lower prices for working families: In May 2026, Tran joined fellow members of the Lowering Costs Caucus in a letter urging the Trump Administration to address skyrocketing energy prices . In July 2025, Representative Tran introduced the Baby Food Tax Relief Act to exempt essential baby feeding products, such as formula, high chairs, and baby bottles, from tariffs to lower costs for hard-working parents. Tran also cosponsored the Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act to finance the building of more multifamily units and the First-Time Homebuyer Tax Credit Act , which establishes a refundable tax credit for first-time homebuyers. ### Issues : Economy & Small Business Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) voted in favor of H.R. 9340 , the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act , to protect Americans from the costs of energy and electrical grid upgrades required to build data centers. “We have a responsibility to be mindful and fully aware of the risks associated with A.I., including rising utility costs for consumers and small business owners. As a former consumer protection attorney, I am deeply concerned that our communities are currently the ones who pay the price for new data centers. The Ratepayer Protection Act protects hardworking families from these costs by ensuring that the data centers are the ones who pay for energy and grid upgrades, not the other way around,” said Representative Tran. The Ratepayer Protection Act was introduced by Representatives Kathy Castor (D-FL-14) and Gabe Evans (R-CO-08), and passed the House by a vote of 417 - 3. The bill requires state utility regulators to establish policies to ensure that community members don’t pay for the costs of building large-load customers, such as data centers, including building new power generation, transmission lines, and other upgrades. Representative Tran is committed to safeguarding Southern California families from the negative impacts of Artificial Intelligence. On September 15, Representative Tran joined a letter with over 100 colleagues to Speaker Mike Johnson, requesting that the House stay in session and pursue urgent action to address the catastrophic risks posed by advanced artificial intelligence. Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran’s (D-CA-45) announced today the successful advancement of bipartisan legislation to protect small businesses against threats from foreign adversaries. Tran helped introduce H.R. 10329 , the Combating Foreign Threats to Main Street Act of 2026 , a bill to provide assistance to small businesses facing threats from foreign adversaries, including intellectual property theft, cyberattacks, counterfeit goods, and other threats. “Small businesses are extremely vulnerable to being targeted by foreign adversaries. It’s no secret that the foreign adversaries, like North Korea and the Chinese Communist Party, are waging an organized global campaign to undercut American influence and steal American intellectual property. To be clear, this bill does not single out any ethnicity or national origin. I will be watching to ensure that the execution of this bill stands in line with its purpose: to protect small businesses because too many lack the legal and cybersecurity resources needed to adequately fight these threats. I’m proud to support this common-sense legislation that connects small businesses to the SBA’s expertise to protect American businesses," said Representative Tran. Introduced alongside House Small Business Committee Chair Representative Roger Williams (R-TX-25), the bill was reported out of committee unanimously. In particular, the bill requires educational material for small businesses that describes potential threats, identifies best prevention and response practices, and provides government resources for small businesses to effectively respond to threats and protect their bottom lines. It specifically focuses on threats from foreign adversaries, including the People's Republic of China; Cuba; Iran; North Korea; Russia; and the Maduro Regime in Venezuela. As a former small business owner and Ranking Member of the House Small Business Committee Subcommittee on Oversight, Representative Tran has remained dedicated to uplifting small businesses in Congress. Tran has co-led several bipartisan pieces of legislation, which passed the House with overwhelming majorities, to ensure that small businesses across the country have the resources necessary to succeed: H.R. 4775, the Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) Foreign Interference Safeguard Act , introduced alongside Representative Don Bacon (R-NE-02) will extend small businesses’ due diligence programs that identify and mitigate the risk of intellectual property theft by foreign entities like the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). H.R. 5788, the 504 Program Risk Oversight Act , introduced alongside Representative Jimmy Patronis (R-FL-01), would increase transparency and efficiency in the SBA’s 504 loan program to support small businesses’ continued access to capital; H.R. 787, the Plain Language in Contracting Act, introduced alongside Representative Nick LaLota (R-NY-01), would require contracting opportunities for small businesses to be written in clear, accessible language; H.R. 832, the Small Business Advocacy Improvements Act , introduced with Representative Roger Williams (R-TX-25), would ensure that the Office of Advocacy of the Small Business Administration represents the interests of American small businesses before foreign governments, and H.R. 1642, the Connecting Small Businesses with Career and Technical Education Graduates Act, co-led with Representative Roger Williams, would make it easier for small businesses to recruit and retain a strong workforce of graduates from career and technical education programs. National security also remains a top priority for Tran. He voted in favor of H.R. 881, the DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act, to safeguard U.S. research and innovation and protect against Chinese intellectual property theft. Representative Tran is also a member of the powerful House Armed Services Committee, overseeing the Department of Defense, and serves as Co-Chair of the House Democratic National Security Task Force. ### Issues : Economy & Small Business Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block;
