WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) issued the following statement regarding the deactivation of Army Expeditionary Combat Aviation Brigades (ECABs) on September 15. ECABs are helicopter brigades that provide essential air support, medical evacuations, and humanitarian support. ECABs are being deactivated nationwide in a modernization campaign; however, this will create a significant long-term capability gap as no replacement will be available until 2032. “It is incredibly disappointing that the Army has gone through with the deactivation of ECAB units across the country. The medical evacuation unit at Joint Forces Training Base Los Alamitos was a critical asset for emergency and disaster relief missions that served communities across Southern California. Deactivating the ECABs without a clear plan for how the Army intends to fill the capability gap will hurt our communities at home and diminish our readiness to respond to global conflicts,” said Representative Tran. “The Army's decision to deactivate the ECABs, including the 158th Aviation Regiment in Conroe, Texas, is an unacceptable gamble with our nation's readiness and puts the future of hundreds of soldiers and civilians in doubt. This decision cuts critical air assault, medical evacuation (MEDEVAC), and emergency response capabilities before a replacement is ready. Our troops deserve better, and the communities that rely on these critical capabilities deserve better. Congress is going to press forward to correct this mistake, restore these essential capabilities, and ensure our soldiers, their families, and our communities have the support and protection they deserve,” said Representative Morgan Luttrell (R-TX-08). Representative Tran has consistently advocated for reinstating the ECABs through the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act and fought for the replacement of these capabilities. The deactivation impacts 150 soldiers and 34 civilians at Joint Forces Training Base - Los Alamitos (JFTB-LA), who have not been given meaningful options to continue their service, causing the Army to lose highly trained pilots and professionals. Tran introduced the bipartisan Prohibit Deactivation of the ECABs Act of 2026 alongside Representatives Morgan Luttrell (R-TX-08) and Jeff Crank (R-CO-05), part of which was included in the House-passed National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027. On September 10, Representative Tran wrote to the House Appropriations Committee leadership to advocate for the protection of flight hours in the Fiscal Year 2027 budget. In a May 15 House Armed Services Committee Hearing, Tran questioned Army Secretary Daniel Driscoll and Acting Army Chief of Staff General Christopher LaNeve about the department’s decision to deactivate ECABs at Joint Forces Training Base Los Alamitos. Tran serves on the powerful House Armed Services Committee, overseeing the Department of Defense. Representative Tran, who represents JFTB-LA in Congress, also completed part of his military training there as a member of the U.S. Army Reserve. ### Issues : National Security & Defense Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) co-sponsored House Resolution 1511 commemorating the 25th anniversary of the September 11th terrorist attacks, honoring the memory of the victims and the courage of first responders, and recognizing the long-term impact of the attacks on the United States. “Twenty-five years ago, our country faced the deadliest terrorist attack on American soil, claiming the lives of 2,977 victims, injuring thousands more, and changing the United States forever. In the 25 years since, I continue to find strength and inspiration in the courage, unity, and patriotism that led our country through the rescue, recovery, and relief efforts. As a nation, we must uphold the highest commitment to stand in solemn remembrance of the lives lost and those who were forever changed on September 11, 2001. It is our duty to never forget,” said Representative Tran. House Resolution 1511 was introduced by Representative Andrew Garabino (NY-02), Representative Dan Goldman (NY-10), and Representative Mike Lawler (NY-17). In recognition of the 25th anniversary of the September 11th terrorist attacks and the long-term impact the attacks had on emergency personnel’s mental health, Congressman Tran introduced H.R. 10329 , the Emergency Responders Mental Health Training (EMT) Act , which expands and improves access to specialized mental health and substance abuse care for first responders. In September 2025, Congressman Tran co-sponsored H.R. 1410 , the 9/11 Responder and Survivor Health Funding Correction Act of 2025 , which would modify the World Trade Center Health Program (WTCHP) to ensure adequate funding until the program expires in 2090. ### Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (D-CA-45) introduced H.R. 10349 , the bipartisan Emergency Responders Mental Health Training (EMT) Act , with Representatives John Rutherford (R-FL-5), Mike Lawler (R-NY-17), and Don Davis (D-NC-1), to expand and improve access to specialized mental health and substance abuse care for first responders. The bill would establish a federal fellowship program to train more behavioral health professionals who understand the unique demands of emergency response work, addressing the mental health crisis that has made it difficult for public safety departments to recruit and retain talent. “As we mark the 25th anniversary of 9/11, supporting our first responders' mental health has never been more urgent. They're on the front lines every day protecting our communities — often at a cost to their own well-being. I've heard directly from law enforcement in my district that access to mental health care remains a real problem. That's why I'm proud to introduce the bipartisan EMT Act to deliver the specialized mental health care our first responders deserve,” said Representative Tran. "As a former sheriff, I have seen firsthand the physical and emotional toll that comes with serving on the front lines of public safety," said Representative John H. Rutherford , "Our first responders dedicate their lives to protecting our communities, but too often, those struggling with addiction or substance use disorders suffer silently. I am proud to co-lead legislation with Representative Tran (CA-45) to expand and strengthen our behavioral health workforce, equipping them with the tools they need to serve the men and women who protect our communities." “Our first responders carry experiences that stay with them long after the emergency is over. Too many struggle to find mental health professionals who understand the unique pressures of their work. We have a responsibility to ensure specialized care is available when they need it. Supporting the mental health of our first responders means supporting the people who protect and care for our families every day,” said Representative Don Davis. “Our first responders put themselves on the line every day to protect and serve our communities. They face traumatic situations, dangerous conditions, and immense stress, and they deserve access to the specialized mental health support they need. This legislation would help strengthen that support by training mental health professionals to better serve our emergency responders. We have a responsibility to make sure those who are there for us in our most difficult moments have the resources they need," said Representative Mike Lawler. The Emergency Responders Mental Health Training (EMT) Act would establish a post-graduate fellowship pilot program to increase the number and quality of mental health professionals trained to assist emergency responders. The fellowships would support post-baccalaureate training, including master’s and doctoral degrees, across fields such as psychiatry, nursing, social work, psychology, marriage and family therapy, mental health counseling, and addiction counseling. The bill authorizes $10 million per year for five years and requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to report to Congress on the program’s implementation and results. The legislation is endorsed by the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI), National Fraternal Order of Police, National Association of Police Organizations (NAPO), Peace Officers Association of California (PORAC), Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association (FLEOA), Council on Social Work Education (CSWE), National Association of Social Workers, Depression and Bipolar Support Alliance (DBSA), American Association for Marriage and Family Therapy (AAMFT), California Association of Marriage and Family Therapists (CAMFT), National Association of Pediatric Nurse Practitioners, National League for Nursing, American Ambulance Association, National Association of Emergency Medical Technicians (NAEMT), and Falck Ambulances Services Inc. “Our law enforcement officers selflessly put their lives on the line every day to serve their communities. The mental, physical, and emotional toll of repeated exposure to traumatic and hazardous situations is an often unspoken but widely understood aspect of the job. First responders are subject to significantly above-average rates of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), depression, stress, burnout, and suicide in comparison to the public. Consequently, this significantly impacts their ability to carry out their duties and, on a wider scale, hinders recruitment and retention rates for the profession,” said Patrick Yoes, National President of the Fraternal Order of Police , “This bill presents viable means to ensure that officer wellbeing is safeguarded so that they in turn can properly protect and serve their communities.” “The work that law enforcement officers do each day and the environments in which they are placed take a huge toll on the human mind, body, and soul. Many of our officers suffer from PTSD and acute stress disorders, but they are reluctant to seek help, especially through services offered by their agency. They worry about confidentiality or believe the mental health specialists provided will not understand what they are going through, what they have experienced,” stated Bill Johnson, Executive Director of the National Association of Police Organizations. “NAPO supports the EMT Act as it will help ensure that officers have access to culturally competent mental health and wellness services. We thank Representatives Tran, Rutherford, Davis, and Lawler for their leadership and support.” “The American Ambulance Association greatly appreciates the recognition by Representatives Derek Tran, John Rutherford, Don Davis and Mike Lawler of the special mental health circumstances facing our first responders, and their introduction of the Emergency Responders Mental Health Training Act to help ensure there are enough behavioral health practitioners trained to support our paramedics, EMTs, police officers, firefighters and 9-1-1 dispatchers,” said Jamie Pafford-Gresham, President of the American Ambulance Association. “Falck strongly supports efforts to strengthen mental health care for emergency responders. This legislation recognizes the unique stressors faced by the men and women on the front lines and helps ensure they have access to culturally competent professionals who understand their experiences and can support their mental health, well-being and resilience,” said Falck Ambulances Services Inc. Spokesperson Jeff Lucia , “Emergency responders dedicate their lives to protecting others, and they deserve access to specialized, trauma-informed mental health care that recognizes the unique experiences of their profession. We appreciate Congressman Tran’s leadership on this issue and his commitment to advancing practical solutions that improve care for the people who keep our communities safe.” "Peace officers spend their careers looking out for everyone else, often at great personal cost — not only through the risks we face in the line of duty, but through the trauma we carry home. Every first responder deserves care from someone who truly understands what this work demands. This bill meets that need, and PORAC is honored to stand behind it," said Peace Officers Research Association of California President Brian R. Marvel. “Social workers represent the largest group of mental and behavioral health providers in the United States. More providers and more resources are needed—now and in the future. CSWE supports legislative efforts like the EMT Act, which will deliver near-term critical support to first responders experiencing mental health challenges, as well as expand training and funding opportunities to train future providers,” said the Council on Social Work Education. As a member of the Bipartisan Congressional Law Enforcement Caucus, Representative Tran has made supporting first responders and their mental health a priority in Congress. In December 2025, Tran helped to introduce the bipartisan CARE for First Responders Act to expand counseling and mental health services for first responders, and has cosponsored several bills to support officer safety and wellness, including: H.R. 309, the bipartisan National Law Enforcement Officers Remembrance, Support, and Community Outreach Act , to improve officer safety and wellness programs; H.R. 3304, the Providing Child Care for Police Officers Act , to support parents in law enforcement; and H.R. 8750, the COPS Reauthorization Act , to provide funding for local law enforcement agencies to hire, retain, train, and equip more officers through the Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS) program. Representative Tran also secured over $1 million for the HOPE Center in Fullerton to deploy licensed mental health professionals alongside law enforcement, ensuring the right responders reach residents experiencing mental health crises while providing more bandwidth for officers to focus on serious crime. ### Issues : Public Safety Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; WASHINGTON, DC - Dân Biểu Liên Bang Derek Trần (CA-45) đưa ra tuyên bố sau khi Hạ Viện Hoa Kỳ bỏ phiếu về Nghị Quyết House Resolution 1490 : “Là con của gia đình tị nạn Việt Nam, những tội ác gây ra dưới chế độ Cộng Sản Việt Nam mang ý nghĩa vô cùng sâu sắc đối với cá nhân tôi cũng như cộng đồng người Việt hải ngoại mà tôi đại diện tại Orange County. Chính vì vậy, hôm nay tôi bỏ phiếu chống House Resolution 1490 - một nghị quyết một lần nữa tuyên bố lên án chủ nghĩa xã hội nhưng lại hoàn toàn không đề cập đến những đau khổ mà cộng đồng chúng ta đã phải trải qua dưới chế độ Cộng Sản Việt Nam. Một lần nữa, các Dân Biểu Cộng Hòa tại Hạ Viện từ chối đưa ra xem xét đề nghị sửa đổi do tôi đệ trình để ghi nhận sự tàn phá về kinh tế, làn sóng hàng trăm ngàn người tị nạn phải vượt biển bỏ nước ra đi, cùng các trại cải tạo đã giam cầm hơn một triệu người sau khi Sài Gòn sụp đổ. Tôi vô cùng thất vọng khi đây là lần thứ hai trong chưa đầy một năm, các Dân Biểu Cộng Hòa tìm cách chia rẽ cộng đồng chúng ta bằng một nghị quyết không thực chất và không đối diện với sự thật tàn khốc mà gia đình chúng ta từng trải qua. Với tư cách là một Dân Biểu Quốc Hội, tôi không ngần ngại đứng lên chống lại các chính quyền cộng sản và xã hội chủ nghĩa ngang nhiên vi phạm nhân quyền. Tôi đã gây áp lực lên chính quyền Tổng Thống Trump, yêu cầu trả tự do cho các tù nhân lương tâm, trong đó có ông Lê Hữu Minh Tuấn. Tôi cũng đấu tranh để những câu chuyện của cộng đồng người Việt hải ngoại được biết đến rộng rãi, để chế độ cộng sản không thể xóa bỏ dấu vết những tội ác mà họ đã gây ra. Hơn thế nữa, các Dân Biểu Cộng Hòa còn sử dụng nghị quyết này để kêu gọi thông qua SAVE America Act, một dự luật làm xói mòn nền dân chủ của chúng ta thông qua những biện pháp hạn chế quyền bỏ phiếu đầy nguy hiểm. Dự luật đặt ra những yêu cầu nặng nề đối với các quân nhân đang phục vụ ở nước ngoài muốn thực hiện quyền bỏ phiếu, đồng thời có thể khiến hàng triệu công dân Hoa Kỳ không thể bỏ phiếu. Thay vì ưu tiên giải quyết những thách thức cấp bách mà đất nước đang đối mặt, các Dân Biểu Cộng Hòa lại tập trung thông qua một nghị quyết nhằm hạn chế các quyền hiến định của người dân Mỹ. Tôi tập trung vào việc mang lại những kết quả thiết thực cho cộng đồng, chứ không phải những trò chơi chính trị nhằm chia rẽ chúng ta. Công việc của tôi trong việc chống lại tai họa của chủ nghĩa cộng sản và bảo vệ nền dân chủ của chúng ta quá quan trọng để bị biến thành một màn đấu đá chính trị mang tính đảng phái cực đoan.” Dân Biểu Derek Trần đã đệ trình một đề nghị sửa đổi đối với House Resolution 1940 nhằm ghi nhận những tội ác của chế độ Cộng Sản Việt Nam. Sau phiên họp của Ủy Ban Quy Tắc Hạ Viện, đề nghị sửa đổi này bị ban lãnh đạo đảng Cộng Hòa tại Hạ Viện bác bỏ. Là con của những người tị nạn Việt Nam và là người Mỹ gốc Việt đầu tiên được bầu vào Quốc Hội để đại diện cho nơi có cộng đồng người Việt hải ngoại lớn nhất thế giới, Dân Biểu Derek cam kết đưa tiếng nói và những vấn đề quan tâm của cộng đồng người Việt lên diễn đàn quốc gia. Trong thư gửi Tổng Bí Thư Tô Lâm vào Tháng Tư, 2026, Dân Biểu Derek Trần yêu cầu được thăm các tù nhân lương tâm đang bị Cộng Hòa Xã Hội Chủ Nghĩa Việt Nam giam giữ để trực tiếp theo dõi tình trạng và sức khỏe của họ. Ông cũng đệ trình một Nghị Quyết Quốc Hội để chính thức tưởng niệm ngày 30 Tháng Tư, 2026, là 51 năm Ngày Tháng Tư Đen. Vào Tháng Tư, 2025 , Dân Biểu Derek tổ chức một cuộc thảo luận bàn tròn với các nhà hoạt động nhân quyền Việt Nam và những cựu tù nhân lương tâm để đưa những lời chứng trực tiếp của họ về sự đàn áp mà họ phải chịu dưới chính quyền Việt Nam đến với công chúng. Là một tiếng nói mạnh mẽ trong việc thúc đẩy nhân quyền tại Việt Nam, Dân Biểu Derek đã đồng bảo trợ và dẫn đầu H.R. 3122 , Dự Luật Nhân Quyền Việt Nam lưỡng đảng, buộc các quan chức cộng sản Việt Nam phải chịu trách nhiệm về những hành vi vi phạm nhân quyền, đồng thời xác lập nhân quyền và thương mại công bằng là những ưu tiên trong quan hệ Hoa Kỳ-Việt Nam. Dân Biểu Derek là người bảo trợ chính thức cho nhà báo Việt Nam Lê Hữu Minh Tuấn, người bị chính quyền Cộng Sản Việt Nam giam giữ một cách bất công, thông qua Dự Án Bảo Vệ Tự Do của Ủy Ban Nhân Quyền Tom Lantos. Ông cũng tiếp tục đấu tranh cho việc trả tự do cho các tù nhân lương tâm trên thế giới. Với tư cách là người bảo trợ cho ông Lê Hữu Minh Tuấn, ông Derek gửi thư cho Ngoại Trưởng Marco Rubio , yêu cầu có hành động hỗ trợ ngay lập tức nhằm bảo đảm ông Lê Hữu Minh Tuấn được trả tự do. ### Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) issued the following statement after voting in favor of H.R. 6500 , the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027, which will fund federal agencies through December 11, 2026: “Today, I voted in favor of a continuing resolution to keep the government open through December 11. While this CR includes important safeguards — blocking the Administration from diverting funds to Border Patrol and halting a rule that would let political appointees interfere with grant decisions using taxpayer money — it is only a temporary fix. Congress must come together on a bipartisan basis to rein in the corruption, provide meaningful oversight, and ensure these agencies are truly focused on violent criminals instead of targeting and separating law-abiding families. I am determined to work with my colleagues across party lines to deliver a funding package that holds immigration enforcement accountable and keeps our Southern California communities safe,” said Representative Tran. ### Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) issued the following statement after the House of Representatives voted on House Resolution 1490 : “As the son of Vietnamese refugees, the atrocities committed under the communist regime of Vietnam remain incredibly personal to me and to the diaspora I represent in Orange County. That is why today I voted against House Resolution 1490, legislation that yet again purports to denounce socialism and yet makes no mention of the suffering our community experienced under the communist regime of Vietnam. Once again, House Republicans refused to advance an amendment I introduced to acknowledge the economic devastation, flight of hundreds of thousands of refugees by boat, and reeducation camps that imprisoned over a million people following the fall of Saigon. I am deeply disappointed that this is the second attempt in less than a year by House Republicans to divide our community through a toothless resolution that does not confront the true, brutal reality that our families lived through. As a Member of Congress, I have been unafraid to stand against communist and socialist governments that flagrantly violate human rights. I’ve pressured the Trump Administration to demand the release of prisoners of conscience, including Le Huu Minh Tuan. And I have fought to uplift the stories of the Vietnamese diaspora so that the communist regime cannot erase its atrocities. What’s more, House Republicans used this resolution to call for the enactment of the SAVE America Act, a bill that erodes our democracy through dangerous voter suppression measures. It places onerous requirements on service members abroad seeking to cast their ballot, and would prevent millions of U.S. citizens from voting. Rather than prioritizing the urgent challenges facing our country, House Republicans are focused on passing a resolution that seeks to limit Americans’ constitutional rights. I am focused on delivering results for our community, not political games designed to divide us. My work countering the scourge of communism and defending our democracy is too important to be reduced to a hyper-partisan exercise.” Tran introduced an amendment to H. Res. 1940 that would acknowledge the atrocities of the Vietnamese communist regime. Following a meeting of the House Rules Committee, the amendment was rejected by House Republican leadership. As the son of Vietnamese refugees and the first Vietnamese American elected to represent the world’s largest Vietnamese diaspora in Congress, Representative Tran is committed to uplifting and representing the Vietnamese community on the national stage. In an April 2026 letter to General Secretary Tô Lâm, Representative Tran demanded to visit prisoners of conscience imprisoned by the Socialist Republic of Vietnam to monitor their well-being. Tran introduced a congressional resolution to formally mark April 30, 2026, as the 51st anniversary of Black April. In April 2025, Congressman Tran held a roundtable with Vietnamese human rights activists and former prisoners of conscience to uplift their firsthand accounts of the oppression they faced at the hands of the Vietnamese government. Tran, a vocal advocate for advancing human rights in Vietnam, co-led H.R. 3122, the bipartisan Vietnam Human Rights Act, to hold Vietnamese communist officials accountable for human rights abuses and establish human rights and fair-trade priorities for U.S.-Vietnam relations. Representative Tran serves as the official sponsor of Le Huu Minh Tuan, a Vietnamese journalist who was wrongfully imprisoned by the communist government, through the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission’s Defending Freedoms Project, and continues to fight for the release of prisoners of conscience around the world. Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) released the following statement in response to the Supreme Court granting an emergency order allowing the Trump Administration to restrict mail-in voting ahead of the November midterm election: “The Supreme Court’s decision to allow restrictions on mail-in voting ahead of the November midterm elections betrays the American people and threatens our democracy. Voting by mail is safe, secure, and gives more Americans the opportunity to exercise their right to vote. Voting by mail helps working parents, people with disabilities, college students, and seniors who face barriers to voting in person participate in our democracy. It ensures that our service members who are serving our country overseas can have a voice in our elections. President Trump knows this, having voted by mail multiple times himself. I am horrified that the Court entrusted with upholding our nation’s highest ideals, including protecting our democracy, is standing by as President Trump continues to sow the seeds of doubt in our elections. I will keep fighting to ensure our elections remain free, fair, and accessible to all American citizens,” said Representative Tran. Representative Tran is committed to securing equal access to the ballot box and cutting through red tape for American voters. In February 2026, Tran voted against the SAVE America Act, which would tighten voter ID requirements and make it more difficult for Americans – especially married women and service members stationed abroad – to vote. In July 2026, Representative Tran sent a letter with Representative Susie Lee to Senate Minority Leader, Senator Chuck Schumer, encouraging him to strip the voter identification amendments within the Stop Insider Trading Act to protect voting by mail. He is also an original cosponsor of H.R. 14, the John R. Garden Grove, C.A. – Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) released the following statement in response to an announcement by GKN Aerospace that it is creating a $100 million fund for families, small businesses, and community members impacted by the hazmat incident and evacuation over Memorial Day Weekend: “Today’s announcement from GKN Aerospace is a step in the right direction. Committing $100 million in grant funding to aid the families, workers, and small business owners impacted by the recent evacuation is part of corporate accountability. This substantial commitment is a crucial and welcome step toward helping our community recover from the severe disruption, unexpected financial burdens, and stress caused by this crisis. Our residents and local businesses showed incredible resilience during the evacuation and they deserve to be made whole by way of direct financial relief to help cover missed wages, temporary housing, and lost business revenue. I commend GKN for stepping up to take meaningful responsibility for the hardship experienced by our neighbors. At the same time, we must recognize that the full economic impact of an emergency involving over 50,000 displaced residents and 5,000 local businesses is complex and still unfolding. While $100 million represents significant progress, I am calling on GKN Aerospace leadership to remain open to evaluating the true long-term costs. If this initial fund proves insufficient to make every affected family and business whole, GKN must be prepared to step up with additional support. Full accountability means ensuring no single resident or small business owner is left absorbing the financial toll of this incident. I look forward to working closely with GKN, local officials, and community leaders to ensure these grant funds are distributed swiftly, equitably, and transparently,” said Representative Tran. On Thursday, May 21, the Orange County Fire Authority reported a leak of methyl methacrylate, a volatile and flammable chemical, from a 34,000-gallon storage tank at the GKN Aerospace plant in Garden Grove. The risk of a toxic leak or catastrophic explosion prompted over 50,000 evacuations across Garden Grove, Westminster, Buena Park, Cypress, Anaheim, and Stanton. On May 29, Representative Tran urged Administrator Kelly Loeffler to issue a disaster declaration and expedite small business loans. The Small Business Administration issued a disaster declaration on June 11, providing small businesses adversely affected by the crisis with access to low-interest federal disaster loans . On August 18, Representative Tran introduced the Hazardous Materials Transparency Act , to mandate that facilities like GKN properly and regularly notify the communities they operate in about the safety measures that are taken to avoid danger to residents and small businesses. ### Issues : Public Safety Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Washington, DC – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) led a letter with his National Security Task Force co-chairs Representatives Jason Crow (CO-06) and Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) to President Trump and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth demanding a full public accounting of the economic costs of the war with Iran as prices rise for American families nationwide. Read the full letter HERE . "What was billed as a two-week operation is now a full-scale war that has lasted for over 150 days, cost at least $37 billion, and claimed the lives of 18 servicemembers. At the same time, prices across the country have gone up significantly, placing the burden of this conflict on American families. By June 9, you had claimed that the war in Iran was almost over 38 times. Instead, the war has continued, leaving Americans across the country with no idea when this war will come to an end and when prices will come down. This uncertainty, and the months of higher costs have taken a toll, impacting Americans’ ability to budget, plan, and save for the future. These costs are untenable, and the American people deserve better," wrote the members. The letter details a request for information on the cost of operations, changes in the oil and energy markets, and macroeconomic impacts. It comes following the Department of Defense’s supplemental request for tens of billions more to fund the ongoing war in Iran and concerns about the risks to the American economy, personnel, and safety overseas. An Army Veteran, Representative Tran is a member of the powerful House Armed Services Committee and serves as a member of the Readiness Subcommittee and the Intelligence and Special Operations Subcommittee. Tran has voted for or cosponsored multiple War Powers Resolutions to reassert Congressional authority over the war, including H.Con.Res. 40 , H.Con.Res. 38 , and H.Con.Res. 86 , and joined the Democratic Veterans Caucus in a letter to President Trump calling for the same. GARDEN GROVE, CA – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) introduced new legislation to require additional transparency and accountability measures for industrial facilities that handle hazardous materials. H.R. 10108, the Hazardous Materials Transparency Act, mandates that these facilities properly and regularly notify the communities they operate in about the safety measures that are taken to avoid danger to residents and small businesses. The bill also requires facilities working with hazardous materials to establish a coordination plan with first responders and to have a community liaison able to provide timely information in the case of an emergency. This legislation was introduced in response to the chemical crisis at the GKN Aerospace facility in Garden Grove that displaced over 50,000 residents and shuttered 5,000 small businesses over Memorial Day Weekend. “The safety of our families and first responders must always come first. The chemical crisis at the GKN facility was a wake-up call that our current oversight of companies handling hazardous materials is simply not enough,” said Representative Tran. “As a member of the Armed Services Committee and an Army Veteran, I know the vital role these facilities play, but they must be held accountable to the communities they operate in. Families deserve to know what risks are in their backyard so they can make informed decisions about how to stay safe in an emergency.” In addition to legislative efforts, Representative Tran successfully urged President Trump to declare a Federal Emergency Declaration on May 25, which unlocked federal resources for air quality monitoring and other emergency protective measures. Representative Tran also successfully urged the Small Business Administration (SBA) to issue a Disaster Declaration, which was granted on June 11. This declaration provided impacted businesses with access to low-interest federal disaster loans. Representative Tran recently visited the SBA Mobile Business Recovery Vehicle in Garden Grove to meet with local owners and ensure they are receiving the technical assistance necessary to recover. On Thursday, May 21, the Orange County Fire Authority reported a leak of methyl methacrylate, a volatile and flammable chemical, from a 34,000-gallon storage tank at the GKN Aerospace plant in Garden Grove. The risk of a toxic leak or catastrophic explosion prompted over 50,000 evacuations across Garden Grove, Westminster, Buena Park, Cypress, Anaheim, and Stanton. On May 29, Representative Tran urged Administrator Kelly Loeffler to issue a disaster declaration and expedite small business loans. Washington, DC – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) issued the following statement in response to President Trump's announcement to substantially scale back joint military exercises with South Korea: "President Trump‘s decision to gut joint military exercises with South Korea is dangerous. South Korea is one of America’s most critical allies in the Indo-Pacific. Reducing these readiness drills serves no legitimate national security objective; instead, it sacrifices vital military deterrence for short-term political posturing and transactional foreign policy. "The consequences of compromising readiness are immediate and far-reaching. Suspending joint exercises emboldens Pyongyang at the precise moment North Korea is expanding its nuclear capabilities and supplying material support to Russia’s war effort in Ukraine. Beyond the Korean Peninsula, this decision signals to allies throughout the Indo-Pacific that U.S. security commitments are negotiable—subject to personal grievances rather than enduring strategic interests. "True national strength relies on credible deterrence, operational readiness, and unwavering commitments to key partners. Weakening our collective defense posture leaves America less secure and erodes global trust in U.S. leadership." ### Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Representatives Derek Tran (CA-45), Ami Bera, M.D. (CA-06), and Salud Carbajal (CA-24) led a group of 65 Members of Congress in urging Secretary of State Marco Rubio to address overly broad and inconsistently enforced Israeli restrictions on dual-use goods entering the Gaza Strip. “Israel faces real security challenges from Hamas and other actors, and we support disarming Hamas and replacing it with an alternative governing entity,” the Members wrote. “However, overly broad and inconsistently enforced restrictions on essential humanitarian goods do not increase Israel’s security.” The letter raises concerns that restrictions are delaying or preventing the entry of supplies needed for medical care, shelter, sanitation, and public health, including ultrasound machines, prosthetic limbs, ventilators, pesticides, pipes, tent poles, and prefabricated structures. The Members also cited a lack of transparency and inconsistent enforcement, including reports that commercial traders have been able to import goods that humanitarian organizations cannot bring into Gaza. “Legitimate security concerns must not be abused to prevent adequate aid to a civilian population in desperate need,” the Members continued. The Members urged Secretary Rubio to press the Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories to publish a comprehensive list of restricted dual-use items and facilitate the entry of supplies needed for shelter, hygiene, sanitation, and medical care. They also asked the State Department to clarify whether it has access to the full list of restricted items and, if so, provide the list and the justification for each designation to Congress. The Members further requested that the Department identify items that can be removed, address disparities between commercial and humanitarian shipments, and explain how dual-use designations are made, reviewed, and challenged. Read the full letter to Secretary Rubio here . An Army Veteran, Representative Tran is a member of the powerful House Armed Services Committee and serves as a member of the Readiness and the Intelligence and Special Operations Subcommittees. Tran enlisted in the Army Reserve at age 18 to give back to the country that welcomed his refugee parents. He served for eight years and was activated for Operation Noble Eagle/Enduring Freedom before earning an honorable discharge. Tran serves as a Co-Chair of the Democratic Caucus National Security Task Force. Representative Tran is a co-sponsor of the Block the Bombs Act , which would prevent the sale, distribution, and transfer of certain ammunition and artillery to the Israeli government. ### Issues : Human Rights National Security & Defense Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Washington, DC – U.S. Representatives Derek Tran (CA-45) and Susie Lee (NV-03) led a letter urging Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer to remove the controversial and unnecessarily burdensome voter ID requirements from H.R. 7008, the Stop Insider Trading Act. In its current form, the bill would both restrict Members of Congress from purchasing new individual stocks and introduce a federal voter-identification requirement. Read the full letter HERE . “[The Stop Insider Trading Act] includes needlessly onerous voter ID provisions that stand to undermine rather than uphold election integrity, particularly as it relates to voting by mail. The focus of the Stop Insider Trading Act should be firmly fixed on doing exactly what its title says it will do, with the voter ID provisions that House Republicans attached to this bill instead debated and voted upon separately,” the members wrote. The Stop Insider Trading Act would prohibit Members of Congress, their spouses, and their dependent children from purchasing new public stocks while in office. On July 20, 2026, the Republican House majority added restrictive voter ID language to the Stop Insider Trading Act. The provision would mandate that in-person voters must present photo identification before submitting a ballot, and any other form of ballot must be submitted with either a copy of the voter’s photo ID, the last four digits of the voter's Social Security Number plus an affidavit that the voter cannot obtain a photo ID, or notarization from a notary public. The bill passed the House with a vote of 232-198, and is waiting for consideration by the Senate. Representative Tran introduced H.R. 7852, the No Getting Rich In Congress Act , which bans trading by public officials and their families and strengthens ethics rules to prevent backdoor deals. He is also a co-sponsor of H.R.3779, the STOCK Act 2.0 , to ban trading and ownership of individual stocks and cryptocurrencies for high-ranking federal officials, their spouses, and their dependent children. Tran is a co-sponsor for H.R. 14, the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act of 2025 , to prohibit voting changes within 180 days of a federal election, require States notify the public of any election rule changes, and hold States accountable for voting rights violations. ### Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Washington, D.C. – Hoy, el Representante Derek Tran (CA‑45) presentó H.R. 9883 , Ley de Responsabilidad Corporativa de Centros Privados de Detención de 2026 , con el fin de responsabilizar a los centros de detención privados que tienen contratos con el Servicio de Inmigración y Control de Aduanas (ICE por sus siglas en inglés) por cualquier muerte injusta de una persona detenida que ocurra en sus instalaciones o bajo su custodia. La legislación permite que las familias de personas fallecidas bajo custodia puedan solicitar compensación cuando las acciones de un centro de detención privado o de sus empleados resulten en la muerte injusta de alguien bajo su cuidado. “Mientras la Administración Trump continúa intensificando sus operaciones de control migratorio de manera imprudente y peligrosa, los centros de detención privados están reteniendo a un número cada vez mayor de personas detenidas, incluyendo aquellas con estatus migratorio legal y sin antecedentes penales. Estos centros se benefician de contratos gubernamentales sin incentivos financieros para mejorar las condiciones de salud y seguridad, lo que ha llevado a resultados devastadores para las personas detenidas y sus familias”, dijo el Representante Tran . “Los centros de detención privados deben rendir cuentas por la negligencia que ha provocado la muerte de decenas de personas detenidas en todo el país. Esta legislación es el primer paso para garantizar dignidad y humanidad, asegurar justicia para las familias y prevenir futuras muertes bajo custodia.” Desde el 20 de enero de 2025, la mitad de todas las muertes de personas detenidas por ICE han ocurrido en instalaciones privados. A la fecha, al menos 53 personas han fallecido bajo custodia de ICE desde el inicio del segundo mandato del Presidente Trump. La Ley de Responsabilidad Corporativa de Centros Privados de Detención de 2026 crearía un derecho privado de acción para responsabilizar a los centros de detención privados cuando sus acciones causen la muerte injusta de una persona bajo su custodia, permitiendo que las familias soliciten daños estatutarios, económicos y punitivos. Para garantizar que la rendición de cuentas no sea simplemente un costo operativo, la legislación impondría un mínimo estatutario de daños de $5 millones, equivalente aproximadamente a un día de ingresos para las empresas más grandes que operan centros de detención privados. La American Association for Justice , la asociación más grande de abogados litigantes en Estados Unidos, ha respaldado el proyecto de ley. El año pasado, el Representante Tran visitó el Centro de Detención de Adelanto para realizar supervisión sobre las condiciones de salud y seguridad de las personas detenidas. Tran, junto con la Congresista Judy Chu y el Congresista Gil Cisneros, fue negado acceso para ingresar y llevar a cabo la visita. Desde entonces, se han registrado cuatro muertes de personas detenidas en Adelanto. Asimismo, se unió a 26 miembros del Congreso de la delegación de California para solicitar al Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS por sus siglas en inglés) y a ICE que investiguen a CoreCivic, una empresa contratista de centros de detención privados, por graves violaciones a los derechos civiles federales y protecciones para personas con discapacidades. El Representante Tran también presentó la Ley de Responsabilidad Constitucional de ICE y CBP para brindar justicia a las víctimas de abusos constitucionales cometidos por ICE, y ha copatrocinado legislación para establecer controles sobre la conducta de ICE, incluyendo: H.R. 4176, Ley Contra la Policía Secreta , para prohibir que agentes de ICE utilicen cubiertas faciales no tácticas mientras están de servicio; H.R. 5973, Ley para Detener el Uso Excesivo de Fuerza en Operaciones Migratorias , para limitar el nivel de fuerza permitido en operaciones de inmigración; H.R. 3172, Ley de Visibilidad de ICE , para exigir que los agentes se identifiquen claramente como tales al interactuar con el público; H.R. 5653, Ley de Confianza a Través de la Transparencia , para requerir que todos los funcionarios de ICE utilicen cámaras durante interacciones públicas en operaciones de control migratorio; H.R. 944, Ley de Acceso a Asesoría Legal , para garantizar que ciudadanos estadounidenses y personas con estatus legal puedan llamar a un abogado o familiar para obtener asistencia legal cuando sean detenidos; H.R. 5941, Ley de Restauración de Acceso para Personas Detenidas , para exigir que DHS permita que personas detenidas contacten a su abogado y familiares; y H.R. 4456, Ley para Detener que ICE Detenga a Ciudadanos Estadounidenses , para prohibir que ICE utilice fondos federales para detener o deportar ciudadanos estadounidenses. Desde que asumió el cargo en enero de 2025, la oficina del Representante Tran ha abierto más de 600 casos para asistir a sus constituyentes en la resolución de asuntos relacionados con la adjudicación de su estatus migratorio ante agencias federales. ### Issues : Immigration Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) introduced H.R. 9883 , the Private Detention Corporate Accountability Act of 2026 , to hold privately-owned detention centers that contract with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) accountable for any wrongful deaths of a detainee that occur in their facilities or under their care. The legislation allows families of deceased detainees to seek damages when a private detention facility or its employees’ actions result in a wrongful death of someone in their care. “As the Trump Administration continues to ramp up their reckless and dangerous immigration enforcement operations, private detention centers are responsible for holding an increasing number of detainees, including those with legal immigration status and no criminal record. Private detention centers benefit from government contracts with no financial incentive to improve health and safety conditions, leading to devastating outcomes for detainees and their families,” said Representative Tran. “Private detention centers must be held accountable for the negligence that has led to the deaths of dozens of detainees nationwide. This legislation is the first step to ensure dignity and humanity for detainees, ensure justice for families and prevent future deaths in custody.” Since January 20, 2025, half of all ICE detainee deaths occurred in privately-owned detention facilities. To date, at least 53 people have died in ICE Custody since the start of President Trump’s second term. The Private Detention Corporate Accountability Act of 2026 would create a private right of action to hold private detention centers liable when their actions cause the wrongful death of a person in their custody, allowing families to seek statutory, economic, and punitive damages. To ensure accountability is more than just the cost of doing business, the legislation would impose a statutory damage minimum of $5 million, roughly equal to one day’s worth of revenue for the largest private detention center companies. The American Association for Justice, the largest association for trial lawyers in the United States, has endorsed the bill. Last year, Representative Tran visited the Adelanto Detention Center to conduct oversight on detainee health and safety. Tran, along with Congresswoman Judy Chu and Congressman Gil Cisneros, was blocked from entering and conducting the visit. There have been 4 detainee deaths at Adelanto since Representative Tran’s visit. He also joined 26 California Members of Congress calling on DHS and ICE to investigate CoreCivice, a privately-run detention center contractor, for serious violations of federal civil rights and disability protections. Representative Tran introduced the ICE and CBP Constitutional Accountability Act to deliver justice for victims of ICE’s constitutional rights abuses, and has cosponsored legislation to place checks on ICE’s conduct, including: H.R. 4176, The No Secret Police Act , to prohibit ICE agents from wearing non-tactical face coverings while on duty; H.R. 5973, The Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act , to scale back the level of force permissible in immigration operations; H.R. 3172, The ICE Visibility Act , to require agents to clearly identify themselves as such when interacting with the public; H.R. 5653, The Trust Through Transparency Act , to require all ICE officials to wear body cameras when interacting with the public in immigration enforcement operations; H.R. 944, The Access to Counsel Act , to ensure that U.S. citizens and individuals with lawful status are able to call an attorney or family member to seek legal assistance when they are detained; H.R. 5941, The Restoring Access for Detainees Act , to require DHS to allow noncitizens who have been detained to contact their legal counsel and families; and H.R. 4456, Stop ICE from Kidnapping U.S. Citizens Act , to prohibit ICE from using federal funds to detain or deport U.S. citizens. Washington, DC – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) issued a statement following the House of Representatives' vote on the National Defense Authorization Act of 2027 (NDAA). “The National Defense Authorization Act has long been a bipartisan process that prioritizes our national security and the health and safety of service members. That is why I voted to advance the bill out of the House Armed Services Committee. Unfortunately, the politicized NDAA package that was voted on by the full House prioritizes partisan talking points over the safety of the American people. “I was disappointed that Congressional Republicans rejected my proposed amendments to prevent the further delay of critical arms sales to Taiwan and prevent future hazmat crises following the Garden Grove chemical incident in May. Our troops and our national security must be the focus of the NDAA. “Bipartisanship is key to this process, and I was deeply disappointed to see the full House change the bipartisan bill that came out of the Armed Services Committee, packing it with partisan priorities and attaching the SAVE America Act, which erodes our democracy through dangerous voter suppression measures. The SAVE America Act places onerous requirements on servicemembers abroad to cast their ballot, and would prevent millions of Americans from voting just because they don’t have a passport. Our servicemembers and their families deserve better than political games, and, as a Veteran, I cannot in good conscience vote for the bill in this form. “This bill invests over $1 trillion in the U.S. military, with billions for President Trump’s reckless war in Iran, but lacks critical investments in the wellbeing of our service members and strengthening of our national security. When so many families across Orange and LA counties are struggling with high costs of living, I will not authorize over a trillion dollars in spending that doesn’t serve the American people. I will continue to seek out every possible opportunity to work with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to deliver for our troops and keep our country safe.” The National Defense Authorization Act of 2027 passed the House following a floor vote of 216-212. Following the hazmat crisis at the GKN Aerospace facility in Garden Grove, Representative Tran introduced an amendment to the NDAA to require additional transparency and accountability for defense industrial facilities that handle hazardous materials, including notification to nearby residents and coordination with local emergency responders about the use of hazardous chemicals. Representative Tran also introduced an amendment to solidify the United States’ commitment to strengthening our national security in the Indo-Pacific after President Trump announced a freeze on a $14 billion arms package to Taiwan. By guaranteeing U.S. arms support for Taiwan, Rep. Tran’s amendment would deter Chinese Communist Party aggression in the region, protect American troops serving overseas, and strengthen partnerships with essential allies in the region. An Army Veteran, Representative Tran is a member of the powerful House Armed Services Committee and serves as a member of the Readiness Subcommittee and the Intelligence and Special Operations Subcommittee. Tran enlisted in the Army Reserve at age 18 to give back to the country that welcomed his refugee parents. He served for eight years and was activated for Operation Noble Eagle/Enduring Freedom before earning an honorable discharge. The first bill Tran introduced in Congress was H.R. 1637 , the Protect Veteran Jobs Act, to restore the livelihoods of Veterans wrongfully fired from their civil service positions. Tran serves as a Co-Chair of the Democratic Caucus National Security Task Force. ### Issues : National Security & Defense Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Washington, DC - Trong thư gửi Đại Sứ Nguyễn Quốc Dzũng, đại sứ nước Cộng Hòa Xã Hội Chủ Nghĩa Việt Nam tại Hoa Kỳ, Dân Biểu Liên Bang Derek Trần (CA-45) một lần nữa bày tỏ lo ngại sâu sắc về những vi phạm nhân quyền của chính phủ Việt Nam. Nhiều bằng chứng đáng tin cậy cho thấy chính phủ Việt Nam đã thực hiện các hành vi như giết người tùy tiện, tra tấn, bắt giữ tùy tiện, hạn chế quyền tự do ngôn luận và tự do báo chí, bao gồm việc bắt giam các nhà báo, đồng thời hạn chế quyền tự do tôn giáo, và quyền tự do và tham gia các tổ chức đại diện của người lao động. Đọc toàn văn bức thư TẠI ĐÂY . "Tôi kêu gọi chính phủ Việt Nam thực hiện đầy đủ các cam kết của mình theo luật pháp quốc tế, không chỉ bằng lời nói mà bằng những hành động cụ thể. Tôi cũng mạnh mẽ khuyến khích hai bên tiến hành các cuộc đối thoại cởi mở và thẳng thắn về nhân quyền, vì đây là yếu tố thiết yếu để thúc đẩy sự ổn định và tiến bộ. Quan hệ song phương Hoa Kỳ–Việt Nam sẽ bền vững, đáng tin cậy và hiệu quả hơn khi chính phủ Việt Nam tôn trọng đầy đủ các quyền và phẩm giá của chính người dân của mình," Dân Biểu Derek Trần viết. Là con của những người tị nạn Việt Nam và là người Mỹ gốc Việt đầu tiên được bầu để đại diện cho cộng đồng người Việt hải ngoại lớn nhất thế giới tại Quốc Hội Hoa Kỳ, Dân Biểu Derek Trần luôn cam kết thúc đẩy trách nhiệm giải trình đối với các vi phạm nhân quyền của chính phủ Việt Nam. Vào Tháng Tư, 2026, ông gửi thư đến Tổng Bí Thư Tô Lâm, yêu cầu được thăm các tù nhân lương tâm đang bị giam giữ tại Việt Nam nhằm theo dõi tình trạng sức khỏe và điều kiện giam giữ của họ. Ông cũng đã giới thiệu một nghị quyết tại Quốc Hội để chính thức công nhận ngày 30 Tháng Tư, 2026, là kỷ niệm 51 năm Tháng Tư Đen. Trước đó, vào Tháng Tư, 2025, Dân Biểu Derek Trần tổ chức một buổi tọa đàm với các nhà hoạt động nhân quyền Việt Nam và các cựu tù nhân lương tâm để lắng nghe và chia sẻ những trải nghiệm trực tiếp của họ về tình trạng đàn áp mà họ phải đối mặt dưới chính quyền Việt Nam. Là một tiếng nói mạnh mẽ trong việc thúc đẩy nhân quyền tại Việt Nam, ông đồng bảo trợ H.R. 3122 – Dự Luật Nhân Quyền Việt Nam, một dự luật lưỡng đảng nhằm tăng cường trách nhiệm giải trình đối với các quan chức của chính phủ Việt Nam liên quan đến các hành vi vi phạm nhân quyền, đồng thời đưa các ưu tiên về nhân quyền và thương mại công bằng vào quan hệ Hoa Kỳ–Việt Nam. Dân Biểu Derek Trần cũng là người bảo trợ chính thức cho nhà báo Lê Hữu Minh Tuấn, người bị chính phủ Việt Nam kết án và giam giữ oan, thông qua Dự Án Bảo Vệ Quyền Tự Do của Ủy Ban Nhân Quyền Tom Lantos, và tiếp tục đấu tranh cho việc trả tự do cho các tù nhân lương tâm trên thế giới. ### Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Washington, D.C. – In a letter to the Socialist Republic of Vietnam’s Ambassador to the United States, Ambassador Nguyen Quoc Dzung, U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) once again expressed grave concern about the Vietnamese government’s consistent violation of human rights. Credible evidence has shown that the Vietnamese government has engaged in arbitrary killings, torture, arrests, restrictions on free expression, including arresting journalists, restrictions on religious freedom, and restrictions on workers’ freedom of association. Read the full letter HERE . “I urge the Vietnamese government to honor its commitments under international law, not merely in word but in practice. I also strongly encourage open and candid discussions on human rights, which is essential to foster greater stability and progress. U.S.-Vietnam bilateral relationships will be stronger, more reliable, and more productive when the Vietnamese government fully respects the rights and dignities of its own citizens,” wrote Representative Tran. As the son of Vietnamese refugees and the first Vietnamese American elected to represent the world’s largest Vietnamese diaspora in Congress, Representative Tran is committed to holding the Vietnamese government accountable for human rights abuses. In an April 2026 letter to General Secretary Tô Lâm, Representative Tran demanded to visit prisoners of conscience imprisoned by the Socialist Republic of Vietnam to monitor their well-being. Tran introduced a congressional resolution to formally mark April 30, 2026 as the 51st anniversary of Black April. In April 2025, Congressman Tran held a roundtable with Vietnamese human rights activists and former prisoners of conscience to uplift their firsthand accounts of the oppression they faced at the hands of the Vietnamese government. Tran, a vocal advocate for advancing human rights in Vietnam, co-led H.R. 3122, the bipartisan Vietnam Human Rights Act, to hold Vietnamese communist officials accountable for human rights abuses and establish human rights and fair-trade priorities for U.S.-Vietnam relations. Representative Tran serves as the official sponsor of Le Huu Minh Tuan, a Vietnamese journalist who was wrongfully imprisoned by the communist government, through the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission’s Defending Freedoms Project and continues to fight for the release of prisoners of conscience around the world. ### Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block; Washington, D.C. – Hôm nay, Hạ Viện Hoa Kỳ thông qua H.R. 8595 - Dự Luật Chuẩn Chi Ngân Sách năm 2027 cho An Ninh Quốc Gia, Bộ Ngoại Giao và Các Chương Trình Liên Quan, trong đó bao gồm đề nghị sửa đổi của Dân Biểu Liên Bang Derek Trần (CA-45) nhằm tăng cường trách nhiệm giải trình đối với chính phủ Cộng Sản Việt Nam về các vi phạm nhân quyền. Vui lòng xem Dân Biểu Liên Bang Derek Trần phát biểu về đề nghị sửa đổi dự luật tại đây . Điều khoản này sẽ phân bổ ngân sách cho Bộ Ngoại Giao Hoa Kỳ để tổ chức Đối Thoại Nhân Quyền Hoa Kỳ–Việt Nam thường niên, một công cụ ngoại giao quan trọng nhằm thúc đẩy chính phủ Việt Nam giải quyết các vi phạm nhân quyền, bao gồm việc giam giữ các nhà báo, những người bất đồng chính kiến và các lãnh đạo tôn giáo. Điều khoản này cũng tái khẳng định cam kết của Quốc Hội Hoa Kỳ trong việc thúc đẩy nhân quyền và các quyền tự do căn bản tại Việt Nam. "Hoa Kỳ là ngọn hải đăng của tự do, dân chủ và luôn kiên định trong cam kết bảo vệ nhân quyền. Khi chính phủ Việt Nam tiếp tục hạn chế quyền tự do ngôn luận, tự do báo chí và quyền bày tỏ quan điểm chính trị một cách ôn hòa, Hoa Kỳ có trách nhiệm lên tiếng phản đối những hành vi vi phạm nhân quyền này. Những tù nhân lương tâm như Lê Hữu Minh Tuấn cần được đoàn tụ với gia đình, thay vì bị giam giữ trong các nhà tù tại Việt Nam. Tôi tự hào khi đề nghị sửa đổi của tôi nhằm buộc chính phủ Việt Nam chịu trách nhiệm về các vi phạm nhân quyền đã nhận được sự ủng hộ của Hạ Viện Hoa Kỳ. Các chương trình ngoại giao và viện trợ đối ngoại đóng vai trò thiết yếu trong việc bảo vệ lợi ích an ninh quốc gia của Hoa Kỳ cũng như thúc đẩy nhân quyền trên thế giới, và tôi sẽ tiếp tục đấu tranh tại Quốc Hội để bảo đảm các chương trình này nhận được sự hỗ trợ mạnh mẽ. Tôi kêu gọi Bộ Ngoại Giao sớm lên lịch và tổ chức kỳ Đối Thoại Nhân Quyền Hoa Kỳ–Việt Nam tiếp theo trong thời gian sớm nhất," Dân Biểu Derek Trần cho biết. Đạo Luật Chuẩn Chi Ngân Sách năm 2027 cho An Ninh Quốc Gia, Bộ Ngoại Giao và Các Chương Trình Liên Quan cung cấp ngân sách cho Bộ Ngoại Giao Hoa Kỳ và các chương trình viện trợ đối ngoại nhằm thúc đẩy hoạt động ngoại giao và tăng cường an ninh quốc gia của Hoa Kỳ. Dự luật được Hạ Viện thông qua với kết quả biểu quyết 217 phiếu thuận và 209 phiếu chống. Là người gốc Việt đầu tiên được bầu đại diện Little Saigon của Orange County và cộng đồng người Việt hải ngoại lớn nhất thế giới tại Quốc Hội Hoa Kỳ, Dân Biểu Derek Trần là một tiếng nói mạnh mẽ trong việc đấu tranh chống các vi phạm nhân quyền tại Việt Nam. Ông là đồng tác giả của H.R. 3122 - Dự Luật Nhân Quyền Việt Nam, một dự luật lưỡng đảng nhằm tăng cường trách nhiệm giải trình đối với các quan chức của chính phủ Cộng Sản Việt Nam liên quan đến các hành vi vi phạm nhân quyền, đồng thời đưa các ưu tiên về nhân quyền và thương mại công bằng vào quan hệ Hoa Kỳ–Việt Nam. Dân Biểu Derek Trần cũng là người bảo trợ chính thức cho nhà báo Lê Hữu Minh Tuấn, người bị chính phủ Cộng Sản Việt Nam kết án và giam giữ oan, thông qua Dự Án Bảo Vệ Quyền Tự Do của Ủy Ban Nhân Quyền Tom Lantos, và tiếp tục đấu tranh cho việc trả tự do cho các tù nhân lương tâm trên thế giới. ### Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Washington DC Office 1127 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Phone: (202) 225-2415 Cypress District Office 6803 International Ave., Suite 100 Cypress, CA 90630 Phone: (714) 960-6483 Image About Issues Economy & Small Businesss Education Energy & Environment Health Human Rights Immigration National Security & Defense Public Safety Veterans Committees and Caucuses Our District Votes and Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Request an Appearance Website Problem Media Press Releases In the News Media Inquiries Press List Sign Up Read My Newsletter Services Garden Grove Hazmat Disaster Resources Get Involved Congressional App Challenge Congressional Art Competition Internships Military Academy Nominations Youth Advisory Board Appropriations & Community Project Funding Requests FY2027 NDAA and Defense Appropriations Requests Tours and Tickets Commendations and Greetings Flags Grant Applicants Casework Assistance Help with a Federal Agency ICE Privacy Release Form Passport Fair Mobile Office Hours Resources Casework Successes Submit your Testimonial - Mass Firing of Veteran Federal Civilian Service Employees Copyright Privacy House.gov Accessibility RSS .paragraph--id--41 { display: block;
